knowledge/concepts/actor-critic.md.title: Actor-Critic
knowledge/concepts/actor-critic.md.description: Actor-Critic methods learn a policy (actor) and value function (critic) simultaneously, combining policy gradient and value-based approaches to enable efficient learning in continuous action spaces. The critic provides low-variance feedback via temporal difference learning while the advantage function reduces policy gradient variance without bias. Major variants include PPO (clipped surrogate objective, de facto standard for on-policy RL), SAC (off-policy with entropy regularization achieving 25-40% higher sample efficiency), and TD3 (twin critics reducing overestimation bias). Actor-Critic forms the foundation for modern RL including RLHF and delivers state-of-the-art performance across discrete and continuous control tasks.
knowledge/concepts/actor-critic.md.summary: Actor-Critic methods train a policy (actor) and value function (critic) jointly using temporal-difference learning to reduce policy-gradient variance for continuous control, with PPO (clipped surrogate loss) becoming the de facto standard for on-policy RL and RLHF. Off-policy variants (SAC, TD3) achieve 25-40% higher sample efficiency through replay buffers and entropy regularization, while extensions like MAPPO enable multi-agent coordination via centralized training with decentralized execution.

chunk_summaries.1.0: SAC combines entropy regularization with off-policy actor-critic learning to improve exploration and prevent convergence to poor local optima, implementing a squashed Gaussian actor policy with dual Q-function critics.

knowledge/concepts/agent-framework-compa.title: Agent Framework Comparison (2026)
knowledge/concepts/agent-framework-compa.description: Agent Framework Comparison (2026) is a technical guide evaluating six LLM agent frameworks for automation engineers building Claude/GPT-powered agents, distinguishing them from generic workflow engines. The Claude Agent SDK (Python/TS) provides native MCP server support and permission-aware tool invocation tied to Claude models; LangGraph (Python/TS) emphasizes explicit state graphs with checkpointing and human-in-the-loop control; and CrewAI (Python) prioritizes developer ergonomics through role-based team mental models. Choose Claude Agent SDK for Claude-ecosystem integration with file tools and MCP, LangGraph for deterministic graph-structured workflows, or CrewAI for simplified team coordination—the decision hinges on model lock-in, required control flow explicitness, and developer experience priorities.
knowledge/concepts/agent-framework-compa.summary: Claude Agent SDK is the native MCP framework for Claude ecosystem work, providing first-class MCP server support and built-in permissions; LangGraph is the control-flow alternative for deterministic graph execution with checkpointing and human-in-the-loop; CrewAI excels at role-based multi-agent teams. Framework selection depends on whether you need MCP tooling, explicit branching, or role composition.

knowledge/concepts/agent-orchestration.m.title: Agent Orchestration
knowledge/concepts/agent-orchestration.m.description: Agent Orchestration is the process of decomposing complex goals into subtasks, assigning them to appropriate AI agents, managing their execution, and assembling final results—going beyond simple chaining to handle dynamic task decomposition, agent selection, error handling, and parallel execution. Technical implementations vary: static pre-defined task DAGs for well-understood workflows, dynamic LLM-driven orchestration for flexible task discovery at runtime, and reactive event-driven patterns for file changes or API triggers. Orchestrators manage resource allocation, progress tracking, retry logic, and context injection tailored to each agent's needs. Use orchestration for tasks too complex for single agents or when optimal task decomposition isn't known upfront; frameworks like Claude Code's Agent tool, LangGraph, and CrewAI provide different abstractions for common patterns.
knowledge/concepts/agent-orchestration.m.summary: Agent orchestration decomposes complex goals into parallelizable subtasks, dynamically assigns them to matched agents, and handles failures with retries—distinguished from simple chaining by dynamic decomposition, agent selection, and parallel execution. Core responsibilities include task decomposition, agent selection, resource management, progress tracking, error handling, and context injection per agent.

chunk_summaries.1.0: Agent orchestration is the process of managing multiple AI agents on complex tasks, with seven core responsibilities (task decomposition, agent selection, resource management, progress tracking, error handling, result assembly, context injection) and three execution patterns (static DAG, dynamic LLM-driven, and reactive event-driven).

knowledge/concepts/agentic-llm-workflows.title: Agentic LLM Workflows
knowledge/concepts/agentic-llm-workflows.description: Agentic LLM Workflows is a pattern for coordinating multiple specialized LLM agents with different models to accomplish complex tasks cost-effectively by routing work based on complexity. Different models are assigned by task type—Haiku (~70%) for simple validation, Sonnet (~25%) for implementation and planning, Opus (~5%) for critical decisions—while specialized agents handle distinct roles in planning, implementation, and maintenance phases. An orchestrator coordinates agent interactions through configurable workflows (simple, complex, or parallel), with efficient context sharing limited to 300-500 tokens per handoff and file references instead of full content. This approach achieves ~70% cost reduction versus always using premium models while maintaining quality through specialized expertise and routing critical architectural decisions to high-capability models only.
knowledge/concepts/agentic-llm-workflows.summary: Routes tasks to specialized agents with model selection by task complexity—Haiku (70% simple validation), Sonnet (25% implementation/design), Opus (5% critical decisions)—achieving ~70% cost reduction through cost-appropriate model matching and orchestrated agent workflows.

knowledge/concepts/ai-infrastructure-bud.title: AI Infrastructure Budget Configurations
knowledge/concepts/ai-infrastructure-bud.description: A decision framework for configuring AI infrastructure across three budget tiers (€15K–50K), balancing on-premise GPU investment with cloud services based on 2026 market pricing. Entry-level configurations use used RTX 3090/4090 GPUs (~€4K on-premise) with €11K+ cloud allocation; mid-range adds RTX 4090 pairs and Threadripper CPUs; enterprise tier enables distributed multi-GPU clusters with enterprise storage. Each tier specifies exact hardware BOMs, cloud burst strategies (TPU v5e for development, H100 for peak training), and performance boundaries—e.g., 48GB VRAM sufficient for LLaMA 13B inference but requiring cloud for larger model training. Provides ROI timelines (12–24 months) and use-case matching to guide teams from proof-of-concept through production deployment at the appropriate scale.
knowledge/concepts/ai-infrastructure-bud.summary: A 2026 decision framework for AI infrastructure across three budget tiers (€15K-20K, €30K-35K, €45K-50K) pairing on-premise GPU configurations with cloud service allocations to achieve 12-24 month ROI. Entry-level recommends used RTX 3090s + TPU v5e development; mid-range deploys 2× RTX 4090s + multi-cloud training strategy; enterprise enables 4× GPU clusters, each calibrated for different team scales from proof-of-concept to production workloads.

knowledge/concepts/automation-workflow-d.title: Automation Workflow Design Framework
knowledge/concepts/automation-workflow-d.description: An ordered set of design decisions that transforms vague multi-system automation requirements (like "when a customer signs a deal in HubSpot, create a project in Notion") into an implementation-ready specification. The framework comprises eight sequential decisions: mapping the process (triggers, systems, data flow, branching, failure tolerance, volume), picking the engine, designing idempotency, defining retry and DLQ policies, establishing observability, managing auth and secrets, defining cost envelopes, and creating implementation skeletons with chaos tests. Each decision constrains the next, and skipping any leads to architectural mismatches (e.g., choosing Zapier while assuming exactly-once delivery). This discipline separates workflows that run reliably for years from those that break frequently, particularly for webhook-triggered flows, scheduled jobs, and queue consumers.
knowledge/concepts/automation-workflow-d.summary: This framework prescribes an ordered sequence of 8 design decisions—from process mapping through cost enveloping to implementation—that must be made before coding any multi-system automation to prevent mismatched assumptions and runtime failures. The core discipline: each decision constrains the next (e.g., trigger type determines engine fit, which determines idempotency strategy), and skipping any step introduces technical debt from day one.

knowledge/concepts/bayesian-inference.md.title: Bayesian Inference
knowledge/concepts/bayesian-inference.md.description: Bayesian inference is a statistical method that updates probability estimates for hypotheses as new evidence arrives, using Bayes' theorem to compute posterior distributions from prior beliefs and likelihoods. The core equation p(H|D) = p(D|H) × p(H) / p(D) defines how to convert priors and observed data into updated beliefs, but exact computation is intractable for real-world models. Approximate methods—Variational Inference (minimizing KL divergence via ELBO), MCMC sampling, and Laplace Approximation—make this practical; Variational Inference's minimized free energy is mathematically equivalent to Bayesian inference, connecting it to the Free Energy Principle. Bayesian inference is essential for uncertainty quantification, multi-agent coordination systems, and LLM reasoning under incomplete information.
knowledge/concepts/bayesian-inference.md.summary: Bayesian inference uses Bayes' theorem to compute posterior probability distributions p(H|D) from priors and likelihoods, but exact posteriors are intractable because they require marginalizing over all hypotheses. Variational inference solves this by minimizing variational free energy F = -ELBO, which is mathematically equivalent to approximate Bayesian inference and forms the theoretical foundation connecting Bayesian inference to the Free Energy Principle and Active Inference.

knowledge/concepts/blameless-postmortem-.title: Blameless Post-Mortem Methodology
knowledge/concepts/blameless-postmortem-.description:
**Blameless Post-Mortem Methodology**

A blameless post-mortem is a structured retrospective after production incidents that identifies systemic contributing factors and drives corrective action (code, process, alerting, architecture changes) rather than assigning blame to individuals. When engineers trust this non-punitive process, they declare incidents earlier, provide complete timelines including their own actions, and engage fully in root-cause analysis—reducing data loss and enabling organizational learning. Post-mortems are triggered by user-visible impact >5–15 minutes, any data loss, security incidents, near-misses, or recurring issues (third occurrence); the document template includes severity classification, UTC timeline, impact metrics, and action items with assigned owners. This methodology matters because it prevents the defensive behavior (delayed declarations, omitted context, evasion of root-cause questions) that occurs when blame is assigned, transforming incidents into durable institutional knowledge rather than one-off punishments.
knowledge/concepts/blameless-postmortem-.summary: A blameless post-mortem is a structured incident review that attributes failures to systemic gaps rather than individual mistakes, enabling engineers to report early and provide complete timelines without fear of blame. The critical distinction: blameless doesn't mean accountabilityless—action items still have owners—but the document focuses on system and process failures that made the error easy to commit rather than naming the person who committed it.

knowledge/concepts/brand-identity-system.title: Brand Identity System Layers
knowledge/concepts/brand-identity-system.description: A brand identity is a seven-layer hierarchical system (positioning → logomark → color/type → grid/photography/voice/motion) where each layer constrains the next, not a single logo. The positioning brief (Layer 1) documents audience, promise, personality defined by three adjectives with anti-pairs, and competitive whitespace analysis. The logomark system (Layer 2) comprises multiple variants (lockup, monogram, wordmark-only, submark) with proportional clearspace definitions; the color system (Layer 3) uses three-tier tokens (primitive palette ~12 hues × 10 steps, semantic tokens, component aliases) specified across eight color spaces from sRGB to device-independent L*a*b*. The positioning brief serves as the constitutional foundation for all downstream decisions; without each layer enforced, brand identity drifts within 90 days of launch because consistency becomes taste-based rather than defensible.
knowledge/concepts/brand-identity-system.summary: A seven-layer constraint hierarchy—positioning brief → logomark → color tokens → typography → grid → imagery → motion—prevents brand drift by ensuring each layer governs the next; skipping layers causes identity decay within 90 days because no standalone design rule enforces consistency. The positioning brief (audience, promise, personality, competitive landscape) is the constitutional foundation that makes all downstream visual decisions defensible rather than taste-driven.

knowledge/concepts/build-vs-buy-decision.title: Build vs Buy Decision Framework for Indies
knowledge/concepts/build-vs-buy-decision.description: A framework that helps indie founders systematically decide whether to build capabilities in-house or buy vendor solutions, countering the default bias to build. It scores six dimensions—distance from core product, time to ship, ongoing maintenance, vendor lock-in risk, vendor cost, and feature completeness—on 1-5 scales, producing a 6-30 total that maps to a recommendation. The framework surfaces hidden costs like security patching, API breaks, and maintenance burden that indie founders systematically underestimate by 2-3x, treating these as part of the build decision. Use it to replace intuitive bias with defensible analysis, ensuring scarce founder attention prioritizes features that differentiate rather than commodity systems.
knowledge/concepts/build-vs-buy-decision.summary: A 6-axis quantitative framework (1–5 per axis, 6–30 total) mapping to build-vs-buy recommendations, designed to override indie founders' ~70%-wrong default to build by scoring: distance-to-core, ship-time, ongoing-maintenance, vendor lock-in, cost trajectory, and capability-risk. Its core insight: in-house systems' hidden ongoing costs—patches, monitoring, team-knowledge-debt—systematically undervalue buying, yet remain invisible until after commitment.

knowledge/concepts/chunking-strategies-l.title: Chunking Strategies for LLM and RAG Systems
knowledge/concepts/chunking-strategies-l.description: Chunking splits documents into smaller, meaningful pieces for embedding and indexing in RAG systems. Recursive Character Splitting uses a separator hierarchy (paragraphs → sentences → words) to preserve document structure, achieving 88-89% recall; Semantic Chunking uses embeddings to detect topic shifts and split intelligently, performing 2-3% better. The core tradeoff is balancing context preservation against noise and precision—oversized chunks exceed model limits and reduce precision, while undersized chunks lose context and create management overhead. Chunking strategy directly impacts retrieval quality, with optimal approaches yielding up to 9% higher recall than naive methods, making it critical for RAG system performance.
knowledge/concepts/chunking-strategies-l.summary: Chunking strategy—how documents are split before embedding—directly impacts RAG retrieval quality with up to 9% recall variance between approaches; recursive character splitting using hierarchical separators (paragraphs → sentences → words) is the recommended default, achieving 88-89% recall while semantic chunking provides 2-3% improvement but at prohibitive API cost.

knowledge/concepts/churn-taxonomy-and-ta.title: Churn Taxonomy and Reduction Tactics
knowledge/concepts/churn-taxonomy-and-ta.description: Churn taxonomy categorizes subscription losses by source (involuntary payment failures vs. voluntary cancellations) and level (account vs. usage), enabling targeted reduction strategies rather than treating all churn as a single problem. Involuntary churn (20–40% of total) is recoverable through mechanical fixes: smart card retries recover ~30% of failed charges, dunning emails 7 days before expiry reduce losses 20–30%, and account updater services add another 5–15% recovery with minimal effort. Voluntary cancellations are addressed through cancel surveys (to categorize reasons: bad fit, missing features, bugs, pricing, competitor), pause options that save 15–25% of cancellers, and downgrade paths that save 10–20%. For solo SaaS founders, decomposing churn by type and implementing these targeted fixes is the highest-ROI move available—dropping monthly churn from 5% to 2% doubles steady-state MRR with the same acquisition rate.
knowledge/concepts/churn-taxonomy-and-ta.summary: Churn decomposes into involuntary (20-40%, fixable via smart retries and dunning), voluntary account-level (pause options save 15-25%, cancel surveys identify missing features), and silent usage-level (engagement-based re-engagement), each requiring distinct tactics—treating all churn identically is the largest unforced error. Quick-ratio (new+expansion MRR ÷ churned+contraction) ≥2 indicates health; at 5% monthly churn you replace your entire customer base every 20 months.

knowledge/concepts/claude-code-workflows.title: Claude Code Workflows Feature — Premade Workflow Integration
knowledge/concepts/claude-code-workflows.description: Claude Code Workflows (v2.1.154+) is a deterministic JavaScript orchestration tool that coordinates multiple subagents for complex, multi-step tasks. It provides orchestration primitives (agent(), parallel(), pipeline(), phase(), log()), supports up to 16 concurrent agents with token budget tracking, and stores saved workflows in .claude/workflows/ with required pure-literal meta blocks. Subagents inherit the session tool allowlist, always run acceptEdits, and the runtime blocks Date.now()/Math.random() for determinism; triggered via "ultracode" keyword, /effort ultracode, natural language, or saved workflow names, with session-scoped resume replaying cached results. Enables reproducible multi-agent orchestration on all paid plans (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) and enterprise platforms (Anthropic API, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry) with transparent token management.
knowledge/concepts/claude-code-workflows.summary: Claude Code v2.1.154+ includes a `Workflow` tool—a deterministic JavaScript orchestration layer that spawns subagents via `agent()`, `parallel()`, `pipeline()` primitives with token budgeting and parameterization—triggered via the `ultracode` keyword, session-wide `/effort ultracode`, natural-language requests, or saved workflows in `.claude/workflows/`. Up to 16 concurrent agents (1000 per run) are supported; the runtime blocks non-deterministic APIs (`Date.now()`, `Math.random()`), and custom agent types are composable as orchestration stages.

knowledge/concepts/common-stats-pitfalls.title: Common Statistical Pitfalls
knowledge/concepts/common-stats-pitfalls.description: A pre-submission checklist of the six most common statistical errors that cause non-replicable findings in published science. Multiple comparisons inflate false-positive rates; mitigation includes Bonferroni/Holm-Bonferroni correction (strict FWER control) or Benjamini-Hochberg (less conservative FDR control for screening studies). The garden of forking paths (unreported analytical choices) and p-hacking (data-dependent stopping) are corrected via preregistration, specification curves across all reasonable analyses, and predetermined stopping rules prioritizing effect sizes over p-values. These documented pitfalls account for most inference failures in published research, making this checklist essential validation before submission.
knowledge/concepts/common-stats-pitfalls.summary: Most published statistical failures stem from six documented pitfalls: multiple comparisons without correction (inflating family-wise error rate to 64% at k=20), garden of forking paths, p-hacking, Simpson's paradox, pseudoreplication, and one additional type. Each has specific detection heuristics and known corrections—Bonferroni/Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, preregistration, sequential designs, causal DAGs—making them largely preventable with proper methodology discipline.

knowledge/concepts/constitutional-ai.md.title: Constitutional AI
knowledge/concepts/constitutional-ai.md.description: Constitutional AI is Anthropic's method for training harmless assistants by using an explicit written constitution and AI-generated feedback instead of human-labeled preference data. The approach combines two phases: supervised learning from self-critique (where the model revises its own responses according to constitutional principles) and reinforcement learning from AI feedback (using a prompted model to evaluate preference pairs, trained via PPO). The constitution—a human-authored set of principles drawn from sources like the UN Declaration of Human Rights—guides both the model's self-critique and the feedback model's comparisons. CAI addresses standard RLHF's scalability and consistency problems by eliminating expensive human annotation of harmful outputs and avoiding rater exposure to harmful content.
knowledge/concepts/constitutional-ai.md.summary: Constitutional AI replaces RLHF's human preference labeling with AI feedback: a two-phase training process where the model first self-critiques its outputs against explicit constitutional principles (SL-CAI), then undergoes RL training on AI-labeled preference pairs (RLAIF), eliminating human annotation of harmful content at scale. This is foundational to Claude model training and enables better helpfulness-harmlessness alignment than standard RLHF.

knowledge/concepts/default-on-unparseabl.title: Default-on-unparseable + early-return makes locale fallbacks unreachable
knowledge/concepts/default-on-unparseabl.description:
A bug pattern where a parser defaults unparseable input to a specific outcome and an early-return dispatcher prevents fallback mechanisms from executing.

In Windows task scheduling, `schtasks` output was parsed for English markers (`Enabled`/`Disabled`) and defaulted to `Enabled` when unparseable; on non-English Windows where both keys and values localize (e.g., German: `Aktiviert`/`Deaktiviert`), marker misses are expected, yet the default fired and blocked the locale-invariant PowerShell fallback. A unit test locked the wrong behavior by asserting the incorrect default rather than verifying fallback routing with realistic localized fixtures.

Unparseable states must return distinct values (Option/None) and route to fallbacks only after all reliable sources fail—not coerce into outcomes at the parse layer. This same pattern risks container-runtime probes, GPU detection, and version-sniffing anywhere best-effort parsing feeds a status dispatcher.
knowledge/concepts/default-on-unparseabl.summary: In `vct-hub/src/boot.rs`, unparseable `schtasks /Query` output defaulted to `Enabled` with an early return, blocking the locale-aware PowerShell fallback (`Get-ScheduledTask`), causing disabled tasks on non-English Windows (where `schtasks` localizes keys and values) to report as enabled. The fix: return `Option<BootStatus>` from the parser to distinguish unparseable from valid states, apply defaults only at the end of the fallback chain, and test against actual localized fixtures.

knowledge/concepts/diagnosing-non-determ.title: Diagnosing Non-Deterministic Results
knowledge/concepts/diagnosing-non-determ.description:
A diagnostic framework for identifying and fixing sources of non-deterministic results in computational pipelines, which stem from one of seven well-documented causes rather than isolated bugs.

Characterize drift magnitude first (bit-equivalent, ~10⁻¹⁵ floating-point errors, unseeded RNG, numerical instability, etc.) to classify the source, then trace by source using targeted diagnostics. Unseeded RNGs are most common; fix by seeding all RNG libraries (numpy, random, torch, sklearn) with a master seed at entry point and passing `random_state=SEED` to stochastic estimators (KMeans, TSNE, train_test_split, etc.).

Essential for reproducible research workflows when results differ between runs, machines, or Python versions—enables systematic root-cause identification instead of guessing.
knowledge/concepts/diagnosing-non-determ.summary: Non-deterministic computational results stem from seven documented sources—unseeded RNGs (most common, >1% drift), parallel-worker seeding, floating-point reduction order (~10⁻¹² drift), stochastic label permutation, numerical instability, and library/hardware/version differences—diagnosed by first characterizing drift magnitude to identify the likely source class, then applying source-specific fixes. The diagnostic ladder prioritizes measurement (diffing outputs across runs) before guessing, catching common false-positives like re-running inherently stochastic steps or confusing cluster-label permutation with actual bugs.

knowledge/concepts/dimensional-analysis-.title: Dimensional Analysis and Equation Verification
knowledge/concepts/dimensional-analysis-.description: Dimensional analysis and equation verification is a set of four independent sanity checks—dimensional homogeneity, limiting behavior, conservation/symmetry, and order-of-magnitude estimation—used to validate physical equations and derivations before submission or numerical evaluation. The core technique enforces dimensional homogeneity (all equation terms must have equal dimensions, transcendental functions operate only on dimensionless arguments) and applies the Buckingham π theorem to reduce n-variable problems to dimensionless groups that collapse the problem space (e.g., Reynolds number, Péclet number). SI provides seven base dimensions (length, mass, time, temperature, current, amount, luminous intensity) from which all physical quantities derive; dimensional errors in equations like Schrödinger's or the diffusion equation become immediately apparent when checked systematically. These checks catch different error classes (sign errors, missing prefactors, wrong exponents) and together form a near-complete acceptance test; building the habit of running all four before submission or trusting numerical results is essential practice.
knowledge/concepts/dimensional-analysis-.summary: Equation verification requires four independent checks—dimensional homogeneity, limiting behavior, conservation symmetry, and order-of-magnitude—since dimensional analysis alone catches structural errors but misses sign errors and dimensionless prefactors. The Buckingham π theorem reduces n-variable physical systems to (n-k) dimensionless groups, collapsing design-space exploration before experimentation.

knowledge/concepts/dpo-direct-preference.title: DPO - Direct Preference Optimization
knowledge/concepts/dpo-direct-preference.description: DPO is a preference-based alignment method that eliminates the need for a separate reward model and reinforcement learning loop used in RLHF, achieving ~40% faster training and ~60% lower cost than PPO. DPO reparameterizes the RLHF objective into a supervised loss where the log-probability ratio log(π/π_ref) implicitly encodes reward, reducing the pipeline from 4 models and 3 training stages to 2 models and 2 stages (SFT → DPO). The method trains only the policy and reference models using a simple supervised loss that compares preferred vs. dispreferred responses under the Bradley-Terry model, eliminating RL instability and reward model drift. DPO is now the dominant alignment method in practice (Llama 3, Zephyr, TULU 2), though it cannot discover failure modes outside its training dataset like PPO can during online sampling.
knowledge/concepts/dpo-direct-preference.summary: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) eliminates the separate reward model and RL loop in RLHF by deriving a closed-form supervised loss where the log-probability ratio log(π/π_ref) implicitly encodes reward signals, achieving ~60% cost savings and ~40% speedup compared to PPO. Its primary limitation is offline learning: it cannot discover failure modes absent from the fixed preference dataset, unlike PPO which generates novel responses during training.

knowledge/concepts/end-of-cycle-dedup-sw.title: End-of-cycle dedup sweep — what to extract pre-tag vs defer to next cycle
knowledge/concepts/end-of-cycle-dedup-sw.description: An end-of-cycle dedup sweep (Track J) systematically identifies duplicate code that accumulates across multi-track release cycles, which per-track discipline misses because no single track owner is responsible for pre-existing or cross-track duplication. Detection is cheap: a grep histogram finds duplicate function names, then triage determines whether each is a legitimate pattern (delegation, domain coincidence, template scripts) or genuine copy-paste worthy of extraction. Extract pre-tag when bodies are byte-identical, the consolidated version exists or is <100 lines, thin delegates preserve existing call-sites, and tests already cover the surface; defer when the change is release-critical with heavy mutable state, would require new tests to validate behavior changes, or yields only future unit-testability gains without reducing regression risk now. This anchors dedup decisions on actual risk rather than duplication count alone, enabling safe consolidation (v0.2.54 extracted three helper families while deferring three large orchestration functions with documented rationale).
knowledge/concepts/end-of-cycle-dedup-sw.summary: Extract duplicates pre-tag when bodies are byte-identical, consolidated implementation exists, delegates preserve external call-sites, and tests pass; defer when code is release-critical orchestration or extraction requires new behavior testing. A grep histogram catches cross-track duplication missed by per-track discipline—v0.2.54 extracted 4 Python `_atomic_write_text` copies and 6 Rust log-truncation variants, but deferred critical functions like `main()` (1591 lines) with documented rationale.

knowledge/concepts/experimental-design-f.title: Experimental Design Framework
knowledge/concepts/experimental-design-f.description: A nine-question checklist that must be completed before data collection begins to ensure experimental reproducibility and prevent retractions caused by poor design. The framework requires explicitly defining the hypothesis with SESOI (smallest effect of interest), correctly identifying the experimental unit (what is independently randomized—cage vs. mouse, plot vs. plant), specifying domain-appropriate controls, and conducting explicit power calculations rather than guesswork. Implementation demands naming the subject, intervention, comparator, outcome, magnitude, and timing in the hypothesis; matching control n to treatment n; and documenting all choices in the Methods section. Skipping any step is a leading cause of irreproducible findings and wasted lab effort.
knowledge/concepts/experimental-design-f.summary: A defensible experimental design requires nine pre-specified decisions—falsifiable hypothesis with SESOI (smallest effect of interest), experimental unit identification, control specification, power calculation, randomization method, and blinding protocol—made before data collection; each omission drives irreproducible findings and wasted research effort.

knowledge/concepts/fine-tuning-technique.title: Fine-Tuning Techniques for Open-Source LLMs
knowledge/concepts/fine-tuning-technique.description: Fine-tuning adapts pre-trained LLMs to domain-specific tasks without full retraining, with parameter-efficient methods enabling this on consumer hardware instead of high-end clusters. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) learns small "delta" weight matrices via AB^T updates rather than modifying all weights—reducing a 7B model's training VRAM from 40GB to ~20GB while adding only 0.7% trainable parameters. QLoRA extends LoRA with 4-bit quantization, cutting memory usage further to 48GB for 70B model fine-tuning (versus 400GB for full fine-tuning), making RTX 4090 consumer GPUs viable. These techniques matter because they democratize LLM customization: teams without million-dollar GPU budgets can now adapt state-of-the-art models to proprietary domains efficiently.
knowledge/concepts/fine-tuning-technique.summary: QLoRA combines 4-bit quantization with low-rank adaptation to reduce fine-tuning VRAM by 8-10x (enabling 70B model training on 48GB consumer GPUs instead of 400GB), making it the practical standard for domain-specific LLM adaptation while preserving inference quality. The core innovation is training only 0.7-2% of model parameters via small delta matrices, eliminating full retraining costs while achieving near-equivalent results.

knowledge/concepts/flashattention.md.title: FlashAttention
knowledge/concepts/flashattention.md.description: FlashAttention is an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that reduces memory footprint and improves speed by computing attention in tiles fitting SRAM instead of materializing the full O(N²) attention matrix. It uses tiling, online softmax (computing softmax incrementally), and backward recomputation to trade compute for memory, reducing HBM traffic from O(N²) to O(N² d / M) and memory usage from O(N²) to O(N). This solves the fundamental bottleneck that GPU compute (20 TB/s SRAM throughput) is ~10x faster than memory bandwidth (2 TB/s HBM), making standard attention memory-bound. FlashAttention achieves 2-4x training speedup, 5-10x memory reduction, and enables 4-10x longer sequences at the same memory budget—essential for long-context transformer applications.
knowledge/concepts/flashattention.md.summary: FlashAttention achieves exact attention with O(N) memory (vs O(N²)) by processing Q, K, V in SRAM tiles with online softmax, delivering 2-4× speedup and 5-10× memory reduction. v2-v4 optimize hardware utilization, with v3 on H100 reaching 75-85% of peak throughput through asynchronous warp-specialized execution and interleaved softmax-matmul pipelining.

knowledge/concepts/function-calling-reli.title: Function Calling Reliability Patterns
knowledge/concepts/function-calling-reli.description: Function calling reliability patterns make LLM tool use production-grade by addressing the non-deterministic behavior of tool invocation that appears reliable only in demos. Pattern 1 uses strict JSON Schemas with `additionalProperties: false`, required fields, and concrete types, enforced server-side by Anthropic and OpenAI; Pattern 2 implements validate-correct loops that feed validation errors back to the model with a maximum correction limit (empirically ~3 attempts suffices). These patterns prevent four failure modes—malformed JSON, schema violation, wrong tool selection, and infinite loops—that would otherwise compromise production reliability. Use them whenever tool calling is critical to system correctness.
knowledge/concepts/function-calling-reli.summary: LLM function calling exhibits four production failure modes—malformed JSON, schema violations, wrong tool selection, and infinite loops—each addressed by specific patterns: strict JSON schemas with server-side enforcement, validate-correct loops (>90% resolved in one correction), and detailed tool descriptions that explicitly state triggers and disambiguate similar tools. The key insight is that frontier models typically need only one correction round for >90% of schema violations on well-defined prompts.

knowledge/concepts/gdpr-eu-vat-lite-for-.title: GDPR and EU VAT Lite for Solo Founders
knowledge/concepts/gdpr-eu-vat-lite-for-.description: This is a practical GDPR and EU VAT compliance checklist for solo SaaS founders with under €50K MRR and EU customers, designed to achieve defensible status without enterprise-level audit requirements. Key compliance items include a privacy policy naming actual sub-processors (Stripe, email/analytics/hosting), cookie consent only for tracking cookies (strictly necessary cookies don't require banners), and a pre-built Data Processing Agreement ready to send within 24 hours when B2B customers request it. GDPR fines reach €20M or 4% of global turnover, EU VAT applies to all digital B2C sales regardless of revenue threshold, and B2B deals stall without a DPA—making this a tractable weekend effort that prevents costly customer rejections and regulator complaints.
knowledge/concepts/gdpr-eu-vat-lite-for-.summary: EU VAT on digital B2C services is mandatory for any seller (no threshold) since 2015, and GDPR fines reach €20M/4% of turnover, but defensible compliance for solo founders requires five operational items: privacy policy naming actual processors (Stripe, analytics, hosting), conditional cookie consent, pre-built DPA for B2B, functional self-serve account deletion purging within 30 days, and 72-hour breach notification process—achievable in ~1 weekend if started early.

knowledge/concepts/generic-per-module-db.title: Generic Per-Module DB Architecture
knowledge/concepts/generic-per-module-db.description: Generic Per-Module DB Architecture is a design pattern using composite keys (project_id, module_id) to store configuration and state for any paid module in launcher.db without module-specific schema changes. Migration 017 introduces the `module_ports` table (primary key: project_id, module_id; columns: port, updated_at) replacing the older per-column approach (e.g., projects.rl_port) that required new migrations and helper functions for each module. This pattern extends to existing tables like `module_installs` and `module_secrets`, creating a consistent generic-table family where modules register rows only when needed (e.g., HTTP-exposing modules register ports). It matters because adding a paid module becomes a pure manifest + container concern with no launcher codebase changes—essential for v0.2.26's goal of decoupled, scalable module extensibility.
knowledge/concepts/generic-per-module-db.summary: Migration 017 replaces module-specific columns with `module_ports`, a generic `(project_id, module_id)` keyed table, enabling the v0.2.26 declarative-action dispatcher to resolve HTTP ports across all paid modules without per-module migrations or launcher rebuilds—eliminating the scalability ceiling of the previous `projects.rl_port` pattern.

knowledge/concepts/graphrag-pattern.md.title: GraphRAG Pattern
knowledge/concepts/graphrag-pattern.md.description: GraphRAG augments standard RAG with graph-structured knowledge to enable corpus-wide synthesis, addressing the failure of chunk-based retrieval on complex questions requiring multi-source integration. The indexing phase extracts entities and relationships via LLM, applies Leiden community detection to cluster entities hierarchically, and generates multi-level summaries for each community. Query execution uses local search (entity neighborhoods + vectors) for specific questions and global search (parallel map-reduce over community summaries) for holistic corpus questions. GraphRAG excels at global synthesis and explainability compared to standard RAG, though at higher computational and latency cost due to LLM-based indexing.
knowledge/concepts/graphrag-pattern.md.summary: GraphRAG addresses standard RAG's fundamental failure on corpus-wide synthesis questions by constructing LLM-extracted entity graphs with Leiden community detection and hierarchical summaries, then answering global queries through parallel-map-reduce over community summaries. The critical innovation: replacing local chunk similarity with community-level reasoning to synthesize across the entire document corpus.

knowledge/concepts/hook-discipline-vct-d.title: Hook Discipline — VCT_DISABLE_HOOKS Escape Hatch
knowledge/concepts/hook-discipline-vct-d.description: VCT_DISABLE_HOOKS is a single environment variable that silently disables all `.claude/hooks/` shell hooks, making each exit 0 without executing its work. Every hook carries a guard (`if [ "${VCT_DISABLE_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then exit 0; fi`) placed after credential-scrub but before execution, with CI-enforced presence across all 36 top-level hooks. This enables one-knob debugging when hooks hang or misbehave, allows CI runners to skip interactive hooks without rewriting workflows, and ensures clean installations (e.g., `VCT_DISABLE_HOOKS=1 python install.py`). Use when debugging hook failures, running in non-interactive environments, or testing without credential/KG-dependent side effects.
knowledge/concepts/hook-discipline-vct-d.summary: The `VCT_DISABLE_HOOKS=1` environment variable gates an early `exit 0` guard in all 36 shell hooks in `.claude/hooks/`, providing a one-knob escape hatch for debugging and CI without config edits. CI regression test `test_hooks_disable_guard.py` enforces the guard's presence in every hook, and the guard sits after credential-scrub so secrets cannot leak even from a disabled hook.

knowledge/concepts/hpc-job-submission-pa.title: HPC Job Submission Patterns
knowledge/concepts/hpc-job-submission-pa.description: HPC job submission patterns define how to submit compute jobs to academic and national-lab clusters across different job schedulers—SLURM (most common in 2026), PBS/Torque (older installations), SGE/UGE (legacy), and LSF (IBM shops). Each scheduler uses distinct command syntax (sbatch/qsub/bsub), directive headers (#SBATCH/#PBS/#$), and status commands; resource estimation follows heuristics: CPU cores scale with parallelization level (1–16+), memory from input data size (3–5× input plus headroom), wall time from benchmarks (2–5× plus safety margin), and GPUs via scheduler-specific flags (e.g., `--gres=gpu:N`). Detect the active scheduler on-cluster with `which sbatch qsub bsub` or module listing; site-specific quirks live in `/etc/motd` or local documentation. Precise resource specification is critical for reproducible research workflows—schedulers kill jobs at the wall limit with no warning, so underestimation causes silent failure while overestimation wastes quota and queue time.
knowledge/concepts/hpc-job-submission-pa.summary: SLURM dominates 2026 academic HPC clusters and resource estimation must be data-driven (peak memory for tabular data ≈ 3-5× input file size; PyTorch overhead 12 bytes/parameter plus activations), submitted via `sbatch` with thread counts pinned to `$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK` for reproducibility.

knowledge/concepts/hybrid-search-keyword.title: Hybrid Search - Combining Keyword and Semantic Retrieval
knowledge/concepts/hybrid-search-keyword.description: Hybrid search combines keyword-based retrieval (BM25 for exact term matching) with semantic search (vector embeddings for meaning-based similarity), merging both result sets into a unified ranked output. The process runs keyword and semantic searches in parallel, normalizes their different scoring scales (BM25's 0-100 range vs. cosine similarity's 0-1 range), and uses Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) to combine results by rewarding documents that rank highly in either method. This captures both precision from exact terminology and understanding from conceptual relationships. Keyword-only search misses synonyms and paraphrases while semantic-only search returns irrelevant results lacking required terminology, making hybrid essential for comprehensive retrieval.
knowledge/concepts/hybrid-search-keyword.summary: Hybrid search merges BM25 keyword retrieval with semantic vector search through Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), normalizing incompatible score ranges (BM25's 0-100, cosine similarity's 0-1) to capture both exact terminology and conceptual meaning in a unified ranked result set. This solves the core limitation that keyword-only search misses paraphrases while semantic-only search returns irrelevant results lacking required terminology.

knowledge/concepts/kg-summary-three-tier.title: KG-Summary Three-Tier Generation Pipeline
knowledge/concepts/kg-summary-three-tier.description: Auto-generated summaries for every KG node, stored in `knowledge/.node_formats.json` and consumed by retrieval clients via a PostToolUse hook triggered on knowledge file edits. The pipeline uses a three-tier backend selection (claude CLI on PATH > Ollama local > ANTHROPIC_API_KEY direct > skip), with Ollama models offering configurable parameters (qwen3.5 for quality, gemma4 for low-VRAM) and 180-second timeouts for large nodes. Title resolution extracts from YAML frontmatter or falls back to the body H1 heading, skipping only when both are absent. Enables efficient hybrid-search retrieval with pre-computed summaries, automating knowledge graph indexing without manual intervention and supporting diverse backends depending on available infrastructure.
knowledge/concepts/kg-summary-three-tier.summary: Auto-generates 2-3 sentence summaries for every KG node and writes to `knowledge/.node_formats.json`, dispatching to Claude CLI, local Ollama, or Anthropic API in fallback order with graceful skip. Triggered by PostToolUse hooks on knowledge file edits, with title resolution from YAML frontmatter or body H1 and cross-platform subprocess fixes for Windows `.cmd` resolution.

knowledge/concepts/knowledge-graph.md.title: Knowledge Graph
knowledge/concepts/knowledge-graph.md.description: A knowledge graph represents entities (nodes) and typed relationships (edges) in a structure that encodes semantic meaning, enabling multi-hop reasoning and traversal over interconnected facts. Entities have properties and types identified uniquely; relationships are directed edges with metadata—representations include property graphs (Neo4j, Weaviate), RDF triples (SPARQL), and markdown WikiLink graphs. Construction ranges from manual curation (high quality, slow) to LLM extraction (scalable, requires QC) to hybrid methods combining both. Knowledge graphs excel where relationships matter most: they treat connections as first-class structures, enabling efficient multi-hop queries and reasoning essential for enterprise AI, RAG systems, and multi-agent coordination.
knowledge/concepts/knowledge-graph.md.summary: A knowledge graph encodes entities as nodes and typed relationships as edges in a structured graph where semantic meaning is embedded in the connection topology, enabling multi-hop reasoning and inference without expensive joins. Unlike relational or vector databases, it makes relationships first-class and supports traversal-based queries, serving as the foundation for enhanced RAG systems and enterprise AI applications.

chunk_summaries.1.0: This chunk introduces a shared Weaviate knowledge graph that centralizes reusable knowledge across projects and transparently merges per-project and shared collection results via an MCP server with deduplication and reranking.

knowledge/concepts/kubernetes-manifest-r.title: Kubernetes Manifest Review Discipline
knowledge/concepts/kubernetes-manifest-r.description: A structured review checklist for Kubernetes manifests in PRs covering security context, resource allocation, health probes, disruption tolerance, and network exposure—applied hierarchically by severity. Security context must enforce least privilege: non-root user, no privilege escalation, read-only filesystem, all capabilities dropped, and runtime default seccomp at both container and pod levels; red flags include `privileged: true`, `hostNetwork`, and unvetted capability additions. Resource requests and memory limits must be explicitly set with memory limit equal to request (Guaranteed QoS class), which protects workloads from OOM-kill during node pressure. Apply this discipline during PR reviews to catch privilege escalation vectors, resource misconfigurations, and scheduling decisions before they reach production.
knowledge/concepts/kubernetes-manifest-r.summary: Kubernetes manifest review follows a 5-level security-first pyramid: security context, resource correctness, probe configuration, disruption tolerance, and network exposure. Memory limits must equal requests for Guaranteed QoS class—the only class safe from OOM-kill during node pressure—while security context requires non-root execution, dropped-all capabilities, and read-only filesystems by default.

knowledge/concepts/kubernetes-resource-m.title: Kubernetes Resource Model — Requests, Limits, QoS Classes, and Eviction
knowledge/concepts/kubernetes-resource-m.description: Kubernetes schedules pods based on CPU and memory **requests** (guaranteed allocation) and **limits** (usage ceiling), determining each pod's Quality of Service class—Guaranteed, Burstable, or BestEffort—which drives eviction priority under node pressure. CPU is compressible (throttles at limit) while memory is not (OOM-kills at limit); requests steer the scheduler, limits constrain runtime behavior. The kubelet evicts pods in order: BestEffort first, then Burstable pods exceeding their request, then Guaranteed pods only if system processes need memory. Critical production workloads must be Guaranteed to survive node pressure from noisy neighbors and cluster fragmentation.
knowledge/concepts/kubernetes-resource-m.summary: Pod QoS class (Guaranteed/Burstable/BestEffort), determined by request-to-limit ratios, drives eviction order under node pressure—Guaranteed pods (requests == limits) are evicted last and are required for production workloads. Memory limits are mandatory to prevent OOM-cascades; CPU limits are controversial as they cause CFS throttling and tail-latency spikes.

knowledge/concepts/launcher-paid-modules.title: Launcher Paid Modules — Supabase Schema (004_paid_modules.sql)
knowledge/concepts/launcher-paid-modules.description:
**Launcher Paid Modules — Supabase Schema (004_paid_modules.sql)**

Supabase schema extension that tracks which paid add-on modules a user owns by adding a `profiles.paid_modules` JSONB column keyed by module slug (e.g., "telegram", "discord"), with activation metadata, license keys, and expiration timestamps. The column is protected by a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that restricts writes to service-role RPC paths only, and indexed via GIN for queryability. Originally designed as the single source-of-truth for the `validate-module` endpoint, but v0.2.33+ moved runtime entitlement checks to a three-endpoint design where the launcher's `tier_cache.module_licenses` is authoritative. This schema remains relevant for org-side persistence of module ownership when Lemon Squeezy webhooks fire post-purchase, avoiding per-module migrations as new modules ship.
knowledge/concepts/launcher-paid-modules.summary: Migration 004 extends `profiles` with a `paid_modules` JSONB column (keyed by module slug, values: variant_id, license_key, activation/expiry timestamps) for tracking paid add-on module entitlements, protected by triggers and mutated only via service-role RPCs (`upsert_paid_module`, `remove_paid_module`). The schema predates v0.2.33+'s three-endpoint validation architecture—where runtime checks shifted to `rl-artifact-url` with server authority—but the column persists as the org-side source-of-truth for webhook-driven post-purchase entitlements.

knowledge/concepts/merchant-of-record-vs.title: Merchant of Record vs Stripe for Indies
knowledge/concepts/merchant-of-record-vs.description: A choice between two legal structures for processing payments: be the merchant yourself (direct processor like Stripe) and handle all tax compliance across jurisdictions, or use a Merchant of Record (MoR like Lemon Squeezy) where they're legally the seller and handle taxes for you. Direct processors charge lower fees (2–3%) but require you to register for and remit sales tax, VAT, and GST wherever you have customers. MoRs charge higher fees (5–10%) but automatically handle all tax compliance and pay you a net amount. Choose MoR if selling to EU customers (saves ~3 hours/quarter on filings) or earning under $5K MRR; use Stripe if US-only B2B; break-even is roughly $30–50K MRR depending on jurisdictions.
knowledge/concepts/merchant-of-record-vs.summary: Merchant of Record providers (Lemon Squeezy, Polar) legally own all VAT/GST/sales tax liability across every jurisdiction where they sell to customers, eliminating your nexus registration and compliance burden. Their 2% fee premium over Stripe (5% vs 2.9%) is economically rational below $30–50K MRR because it costs less than quarterly EU MOSS filings, 45-state US nexus compliance, and accountant hours that a solo founder would otherwise incur.

knowledge/concepts/model-context-protoco.title: Model Context Protocol
knowledge/concepts/model-context-protoco.description: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard from Anthropic that standardizes how AI models connect to external data sources, tools, and services through a unified client-server architecture, eliminating the need for bespoke integrations. MCP defines three core primitives—**tools** (LLM-callable functions), **resources** (data sources), and **prompts** (templates)—transported via stdio (local) or HTTP+SSE (remote), with a security model that restricts server access to conversation history and requires explicit LLM decisions before executing operations. Implementation uses frameworks like FastMCP (Python) and configuration in `~/.claude.json`, with a straightforward protocol flow: client initializes, lists capabilities, invokes tools, and receives results. This matters because it enables extensible AI applications with external capabilities in a standardized, secure way rather than maintaining custom integrations for each service.
knowledge/concepts/model-context-protoco.summary: MCP is Anthropic's open standard (Nov 2024) that replaces bespoke AI integrations with a unified client-server protocol for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to language models via JSON-RPC 2.0. It supports local (stdio) and remote (HTTP/SSE) communication with Python (FastMCP) and TypeScript SDKs.

knowledge/concepts/model-quantization.md.title: Model Quantization
knowledge/concepts/model-quantization.md.description: Model quantization reduces neural network weights and activations to lower numerical precision (INT8, INT4) to decrease memory footprint, accelerate inference, and lower power consumption. It maps high-precision values (FP32/BF16) to lower-precision representations across weights, activations, and KV cache, with memory scaling as (params in B) × (bits / 8)—a 7B model drops from ~14 GB at FP16 to ~3.5 GB at INT4. Two approaches exist: Post-Training Quantization (GPTQ, AWQ, GGUF, bitsandbytes) applied after training in 5–30 minutes with 90–95% accuracy retention, and Quantization-Aware Training integrating quantization during training to recover up to 96% accuracy but requiring 2–4 hours compute per 7B model. Quantization is essential for deploying large models on resource-constrained hardware; method choice depends on accuracy requirements, calibration data availability, and deployment targets (CPU vs. GPU).
knowledge/concepts/model-quantization.md.summary: Quantization reduces neural network precision (FP32→INT4/INT2) to shrink model footprint (7B model: ~14 GB FP16 → ~3.5 GB INT4) and accelerate inference. Post-training quantization (GPTQ/AWQ/GGUF) deploys in 5–30 minutes with 90–95% quality retention, while quantization-aware training requires 2–4 hours of compute but recovers more accuracy degradation.

chunk_summaries.1.0: This chunk presents a three-step decision framework for quantizing models: establishing acceptable quality loss by use case, assessing VRAM constraints for RTX 4080 Super (16 GB), and selecting the appropriate quantization method (NF4, AWQ, GPTQ, GGUF, Ollama).

knowledge/concepts/module-contributed-gu.title: Module-Contributed GUI Tabs Framework
knowledge/concepts/module-contributed-gu.description:
**Module-Contributed GUI Tabs Framework**

The Module-Contributed GUI Tabs Framework (v0.2.20+) lets installed modules declare configuration tabs in their `vct-module.json` that the launcher renders in the sidebar without bundling Svelte components or rebuilding the binary. Modules define a JSON schema under `gui.config_tab` with sections and control variants (Checkbox, MultiSelect, Button, Select, Info), each carrying optional tooltips, validated by Rust at load time. The launcher's Svelte 5 renderer dispatches on control kind from a fixed widget palette, ensuring type safety and consistent UX across all module configurations. This schema-based approach eliminates per-module build overhead, maintains Tauri's security model (no dynamic JS), and enables extensible configuration UI while keeping the widget palette curated for realistic use cases.
knowledge/concepts/module-contributed-gu.summary: Modules declare configuration tabs via JSON in `vct-module.json` that the launcher auto-renders into the sidebar without requiring bundled Svelte components or binary rebuilds. Schema-rendered controls (checkbox, button, select, multi-select, info) eliminate per-module build overhead while enforcing type safety and first-class tooltip support through the manifest.

knowledge/concepts/motion-principles-for.title: Motion Principles for UI
knowledge/concepts/motion-principles-for.description: Motion in UI is a communication channel—not decoration—that uses animated transitions to convey spatial and state information by answering four core questions: where did this come from, where did it go, what's happening now, and what just changed. Disney animation principles adapted to UI include spring physics for natural feel, hover states for anticipation, and staggered timing to guide focal hierarchy; pose-to-pose keyframing lets designers define states while the runtime interpolates the transition. Overlapping micro-motions (shadows lingering, adjacent items rippling) create physical realism, while easing curves replace rigid linear motion to simulate natural acceleration and deceleration. Well-executed motion makes UIs feel alive and responsive; poor motion slows users down, triggers accessibility issues, and reads as self-indulgent—every motion must serve one of the four communication purposes or be eliminated.
knowledge/concepts/motion-principles-for.summary: Motion in UI is a communication channel answering four questions—where elements come from, where they go, what's happening now, and what changed—implemented via Disney animation principles adapted with spring physics, easing curves, and staggered staging, prioritizing these functional goals over aesthetic decoration.

knowledge/concepts/neurosymbolic-ai.md.title: Neurosymbolic AI
knowledge/concepts/neurosymbolic-ai.md.description: Neurosymbolic AI integrates neural networks (pattern recognition from raw data) with symbolic reasoning (interpretable logic) to overcome each paradigm's limitations—combining data-driven learning with systematic, compositional reasoning. A unifying measure-theoretic formalism models this as F(φ; θ) = ∫_Ω l(φ, ω) · b_θ(ω) dμ(ω), where logical satisfaction l and neural beliefs b_θ integrate over possible interpretations, enabling end-to-end differentiation through both components. Key architectures include Logical Tensor Networks (grounding first-order logic in differentiable t-norms), DeepProbLog (neural predicates in probabilistic logic programs), and Neural Logic Programming (learning rules as differentiable embeddings). Use this for knowledge-constrained learning, structured prediction, and reasoning tasks requiring both data-driven perception and explicit logical constraints.
knowledge/concepts/neurosymbolic-ai.md.summary: Neurosymbolic AI integrates neural networks with symbolic reasoning via a unified measure-theoretic formalism F(φ; θ) = ∫_Ω l(φ, ω) · b_θ(ω) dμ(ω) that scores logical formulas against neural belief distributions, unifying weighted model counting, fuzzy logic, and probabilistic logic programming. Key architectures (Logical Tensor Networks, DeepProbLog, Neural Logic Programming, NSCL) implement this by grounding predicates into differentiable tensor operations, enabling end-to-end gradient-based learning of both perception and compositional reasoning.

knowledge/concepts/oauth2-flow-decision-.title: OAuth2 Flow Decision Tree
knowledge/concepts/oauth2-flow-decision-.description: OAuth2 Flow Decision Tree is a decision framework for selecting the correct OAuth2 flow by answering two questions—who owns the protected resource (end user vs. organization) and what can securely hold secrets (server vs. browser vs. CLI). Authorization Code + PKCE is the standard for user-delegated flows in 2026, involving code_verifier generation (43-128 random chars), code_challenge sent during redirect authorization, user consent, and token exchange; Client Credentials handles service-to-service flows via direct credential exchange. Alternative flows include Device Authorization Grant for CLI/IoT (user types code on phone), JWT Bearer for service account patterns, and platform-native identity (AWS IAM, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) for cloud workloads instead of static credentials. Selecting the wrong flow forces architectural rewrites; implementation critically requires using battle-tested libraries (not hand-rolling), encrypting refresh tokens at rest, enforcing CSRF protection via state parameter, and treating client secrets as database-grade secrets.
knowledge/concepts/oauth2-flow-decision-.summary: OAuth2 flow selection is determined by resource ownership (user-delegated vs. machine-to-machine) and client environment (server/browser/CLI); Authorization Code with PKCE is mandatory for all authorization-code flows per OAuth 2.1 and is the standard for user-delegated access, while Client Credentials and Device Authorization Grant handle service-to-service and CLI/IoT flows respectively.

knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-context-.title: Orchestrator Context Management
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-context-.description: Context management preserves Claude's working state across context compaction events and session restarts through a two-layer memory architecture with automated save/restore pipeline. Layer 1 (MEMORY.md) stores stable facts auto-loaded at session start with a 200-line hard cap (machine-local), while Layer 2 (CONTEXT_STATE.md) maintains active task state in git with a 250-350 line soft target, tracking current phase, completed steps, blockers, and modified files. The system uses Lost-In-The-Middle ordering to position critical information at context boundaries and context-size-check hooks to warn when state approaches limits. This matters because Claude Code auto-compacts long conversations and would lose active task state without intervention, enabling coherent multi-phase work across sessions and team collaboration.
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-context-.summary: The orchestrator implements a two-layer memory architecture (MEMORY.md for stable facts, CONTEXT_STATE.md for active task state) with PreCompact/PostCompact hooks that automatically save working context before compaction and reinject it using Lost-In-The-Middle ordering to preserve coherence across session restarts. The critical mechanism is CONTEXT_STATE.md's soft 250-350 line cap in git, which tracks current phase, blockers, and modified files to restore full working state when Claude resumes after context compaction.

knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-hook-sys.title: Orchestrator Hook System
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-hook-sys.description: The hook system intercepts Claude Code lifecycle events (session start, tool use, file edits, compaction, stop) to automate workflow orchestration with built-in security, knowledge-graph sync, cost tracking, and context preservation. Hooks are shell scripts registered in `.claude/settings.json` that bind to ~20 lifecycle events with optional tool matchers; blocking hooks abort operations, non-blocking ones run async or fire-and-forget. Execution flows through PreToolUse (security scans, logging), PostToolUse (KG sync, linting), Stop (cost tracking), and a compaction path with PreCompact/PostCompact hooks that reinject context during SessionStart. This matters because it enables autonomous workflows where security enforcement, knowledge management, quality gates, and developer experience automation (formatting, type-checking) run transparently without manual intervention.
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-hook-sys.summary: Hooks are shell scripts in `.claude/settings.json` that intercept ~20 Claude Code lifecycle events (session start, tool use, file edits, compaction, stop) to enable automated workflow orchestration via security enforcement, knowledge-graph sync, cost tracking, and context preservation. Lost-In-The-Middle (LITM) ordering during compaction reinjects critical state (`.claude/CONTEXT_STATE.md`) at payload boundaries to preserve context through model context-window exhaustion.

knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-knowledg.title: Orchestrator Knowledge Graph
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-knowledg.description: The Knowledge Graph is the orchestrator's persistent long-term memory, storing architectural decisions, tool documentation, patterns, and research findings as Obsidian-compatible markdown files synced to a Weaviate vector database for semantic search. Every node is a markdown file with YAML frontmatter (title, type, tags, timestamps, status) and uses typed WikiLinks (uses::, implements::, extends::, buildsOn::, relatedTo::) to maintain an acyclic, unidirectional graph structure. The KG serves dual audiences—humans browsing/editing .md files in a folder hierarchy (projects/, concepts/, tools/, models/, hardware/, research/, coordination/), and Claude querying via MCP tools for semantic and hybrid search. This "write once, search everywhere" design prevents rediscovery of patterns and decisions across sessions, ensuring accumulated knowledge is reusable and discoverable.
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-knowledg.summary: The Knowledge Graph is the orchestrator's long-term memory that stores architectural decisions, patterns, and research as Obsidian markdown files with YAML frontmatter and typed WikiLinks, automatically syncing to Weaviate vector DB via Ollama embeddings for semantic search across both human editors and MCP clients.

knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-mcp-serv.title: Orchestrator MCP Servers
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-mcp-serv.description: The orchestrator ships MCP servers that extend Claude Code with semantic search and knowledge graph capabilities, running as native Python processes in a shared virtual environment. The primary server, weaviate-kg, manages Knowledge Graph, Code Graph, and development-documentation collections using Weaviate with Ollama embeddings, exposing semantic search tools like hybrid_search (combining BM25 keyword + vector similarity) and semantic_graph_search. Companion servers provide academic paper search and diagram extraction, while a code-embedding HTTP service on port 11440 powers the embedding infrastructure. This enables contextual semantic search of code and documentation rather than keyword matching alone, allowing Claude to understand project structure and cross-reference information efficiently.
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-mcp-serv.summary: Orchestrator MCP servers (primarily weaviate-kg) run as native Python processes managing semantic search via hybrid BM25+vector fusion with GraphRAG traversal across Weaviate-backed knowledge graphs and code graphs using qwen3-embedding:0.6b embeddings via Ollama. Additional servers provide academic paper search (search), diagram processing (mermaid/excalidraw), and browser automation (playwright).

knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-rl-retri.title: Orchestrator RL Retrieval
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-rl-retri.description: The RL retrieval system is a pro-tier reinforcement-learning reranker that wraps Weaviate searches, over-fetching candidates and reranking them based on learned relevance signals with online training after each search. Each project runs its own isolated RL server instance to prevent cross-project data leakage, with project-specific ports stored in settings.json and feature-gated via license validation that shorts-circuits to standard hybrid search on free tier or when license validation is offline >3 days. The RL server source ships as a GHCR container image (not in the public AGPL repo) and is pulled via short-lived per-user tokens after Pro tier verification, with weekly model-weight rotation serving as an anti-piracy measure. Use this system when you need improved search relevance on paid tiers; per-project isolation prevents mode-collapse that a single shared network would suffer.
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-rl-retri.summary: Pro-tier RL Retrieval wraps Weaviate searches with a per-project reinforcement-learning reranker trained on each project's citation patterns, distributed via GHCR container images with licensing enforced by short-lived per-user pull tokens. Each isolated neural network instance continuously fine-tunes on the last 30 days of search events, degrades to standard hybrid search on free tier or offline license validation, and weights rotate weekly as an anti-piracy mechanism.

knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-security.title: Orchestrator Security Model
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-security.description: The orchestrator implements a seven-layer defense-in-depth security model automatically enforced via hooks, targeting credential leakage, SSRF attacks, command injection, accidental overwrites, and credential commits without requiring user compliance. Key implementations include environment variable scrubbing before subprocess spawning, SSRF guards blocking requests to private/internal IP ranges (10.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16, etc.) with a whitelist for localhost services, shell injection scanning, and file backup for destructive edits. Each layer operates independently as PreToolUse or PostToolUse hooks, so failure of one layer leaves others active. This matters because it protects against prompt injection, compromised tool calls, and supply chain threats—critical safeguards for an AI agent with file system and network access.
knowledge/concepts/orchestrator-security.summary: The orchestrator implements seven automated security layers via PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks; Layer 1 (environment scrubbing) prevents credential exfiltration by unsetting API keys and AWS secrets before subprocess execution, followed by SSRF filtering, shell injection scanning, build anchors, backups, credential detection, and permission controls—each independently defending against a distinct threat, with failures at any layer still leaving others intact.

knowledge/concepts/parallel-agent-worktr.title: Parallel-agent worktree isolation discipline
knowledge/concepts/parallel-agent-worktr.description: Parallel-agent worktree isolation is a discipline ensuring that multiple Claude Code subagents dispatched concurrently each operate in physically separate git checkout directories via the `isolation: worktree` parameter. The harness should call `git worktree add` per subagent to create isolated checkouts, but agents can defeat isolation by `cd`-ing to the parent directory and committing there, causing concurrent git operations to clobber each other's branches and commits. Defense requires three layers: trusting the harness's worktree isolation enforcement, adding defensive prompt boilerplate that verifies CWD and branch before any commit, and conducting pre/post-dispatch audits by the parent to catch conflicts. This discipline is essential for parallel multi-agent work because uncontrolled concurrent git operations require costly cherry-pick + force-reset cleanups and risk commits landing on wrong branches.
knowledge/concepts/parallel-agent-worktr.summary: Parallel subagents with `isolation: worktree` fail if agents `cd` to the parent checkout mid-session, causing concurrent commits to clobber each other and swap HEAD between agents. Defense requires three layers: trust the harness isolation, embed verification boilerplate (pwd/branch checks before each commit), and audit worktree/branch counts before and after dispatch.

knowledge/concepts/physical-constants-qu.title: Physical Constants Quick Reference
knowledge/concepts/physical-constants-qu.description: A reference table of fundamental SI physical constants and derived combinations, values given to 5–6 significant figures based on CODATA 2022 recommendations. Covers ~20 base constants (speed of light, Planck constant, Boltzmann constant, gravitational constant, etc.) plus memorized combinations like k_B·T at 300 K (≈25.85 meV), ℏc (≈197.3 MeV·fm), and photon energy–wavelength relations (hc ≈ 1240 eV·nm) designed to catch common order-of-magnitude errors. Many constants are now exact by 2019 SI redefinition (c, h, k_B, e, N_A). Use for quick sanity checks across thermal, quantum, nuclear, and atomic scales; consult scipy.constants or astropy.constants for publication-grade precision.
knowledge/concepts/physical-constants-qu.summary: Reference of CODATA 2022 physical constants (5–6 sig figs) with curated thermal and quantum combinations ($k_B T \approx 26$ meV at 300 K, $\hbar c \approx 197$ MeV·fm) and unit conversions optimized to catch order-of-magnitude errors in calculations; includes tables of exact-by-definition constants since 2019 SI redefinition (Planck, Boltzmann, Avogadro, elementary charge).

knowledge/concepts/postmortem-authoring-.title: Postmortem Authoring Discipline
knowledge/concepts/postmortem-authoring-.description: Postmortem authoring discipline is the technical practice of writing incident postmortems that drive concrete behavioral change, distinct from the cultural blameless framing that enables it. It counters three failure modes: narratives that describe events without explaining systems, assigning root cause to individuals rather than systemic factors, and vague action items that lack ownership and measurement. The core discipline uses a UTC-timestamped timeline as the document spine, distinguishes observations from actions, includes failed hypotheses as evidence gaps, and frames incidents as intersections of contributing factors rather than singular causes. This ensures postmortems produce action items concrete enough that a new engineer reading it a year later understands what changed and why, converting postmortems from shelf-ware into drivers of systemic improvement.
knowledge/concepts/postmortem-authoring-.summary: Postmortem documents must yield action items concrete enough for future engineers to understand years later; counter three failure modes (narrative-only, person-blame, vague fixes) through UTC-timestamped timelines including dead hypotheses and contributing-factor analysis that stops at system/process level, never person.

knowledge/concepts/power-analysis-sample.title: Power Analysis and Sample Size Estimation
knowledge/concepts/power-analysis-sample.description: Power analysis determines the sample size needed to detect a specified effect size with target probability (typically 80% power at α=0.05), or conversely, the minimum detectable effect for a given n—preventing resource waste and subject risk from underpowered studies. The calculation requires five inputs: SESOI (smallest effect of interest), variability estimate (SD), significance threshold, power target, and test type; without a variance estimate, run a pilot study. Common approximations include n ≈ 16/d² per group for two-sample t-tests and n_paired ≈ (1−ρ)·n_unpaired for correlated designs, where ρ is the within-subject correlation. Use power analysis in study planning to ensure adequate sample sizes for the effects you aim to detect, and in retrospective design to interpret what effects your completed study could realistically have identified.
knowledge/concepts/power-analysis-sample.summary: Power analysis requires five essential inputs (SESOI, variability estimate, α, power target 1-β, and test type); for two independent groups the closed-form approximation is n ≈ 16/d² per group at α=0.05 and 80% power, but simulation is necessary for mixed-effects, adaptive, longitudinal, or complex multiple-comparison designs.

knowledge/concepts/ppo-improvements-st-p.title: PPO Improvements - SORL and Modern Variants
knowledge/concepts/ppo-improvements-st-p.description: SORL (Stabilizing Off-policy Reinforcement Learning) fixes PPO instability in multi-turn LLM agent training by aggregating credit assignment at the turn level instead of per-token, and by explicitly normalizing clipping-induced bias in gradient updates. Turn-level importance sampling uses geometric means of per-token probability ratios (normalized by turn length) to reduce variance since tokens in the same turn share aggregated advantage estimates. Clipping-triggered normalization directly downweights off-policy outliers during training, preventing the exponential growth of clipping bias that causes gradient spikes and collapse. Use SORL when training reasoning agents with sparse delayed rewards where vanilla PPO fails—its two instantiations are SO-PPO (with critic) and SO-GRPO (critic-free).
knowledge/concepts/ppo-improvements-st-p.summary: SORL fixes PPO training collapse on multi-turn LLM tasks by replacing token-level importance sampling with turn-level geometric-mean weighting (normalized by turn length to aggregate advantages at turn granularity) and adding clipping-triggered normalization to downweight off-policy outliers. On multi-turn search benchmarks, SO-PPO achieves 85% success vs. 20% for vanilla PPO by reducing variance through structured credit assignment and conservative reweighting of extreme probability ratios.

knowledge/concepts/process-reward-models.title: Process Reward Models
knowledge/concepts/process-reward-models.description: Process Reward Models (PRMs) evaluate the correctness of intermediate reasoning steps in multi-step solutions rather than only final answers, providing step-level supervision signals and error localization. OpenAI's 2023 study achieved 78.2% accuracy on MATH problems using PRM800K (800,000 step-level labels), significantly outperforming outcome-based approaches; subsequent research identified that human annotation and LLM-as-judge training outperform Monte Carlo estimation. PRMs solve the "correct answer, wrong reasoning" problem by detecting mid-reasoning errors and providing dense, clean training signals instead of sparse end-of-rollout rewards. They are essential for complex reasoning tasks because they train models on genuine mathematical competence rather than spurious answer-chasing shortcuts.
knowledge/concepts/process-reward-models.summary: Process Reward Models evaluate step-level reasoning correctness rather than final answers alone, achieving 78.2% vs 56% accuracy on MATH problems—but effectiveness critically depends on training data quality, as Monte Carlo estimation-based labels significantly underperform LLM-as-judge or consensus filtering methods.
