chunk_summaries.1.0: This chunk contrasts Outcome Reward Models (ORMs)—which evaluate only final answers—with Process Reward Models (PRMs)—which provide step-level feedback on intermediate reasoning to enable better credit assignment and generalization to novel problems.

knowledge/concepts/project-extra-codegra.title: Project-extra codegraph paths
knowledge/concepts/project-extra-codegra.description: A mechanism to index additional read-only filesystem paths into a project's codegraph collection without registering them as launcher projects, enabling code queries across related repositories like a public sibling clone from a private fork. The system spans multiple layers: a database table tracking extra paths, launcher commands with per-project mutex serialization, a Hub resolver endpoint, GUI components, and an analyzer CLI with repeatable `--extra-path` flags that accumulate all paths into a single `visited_uuids` set. The critical invariant requires `--prune-stale` operations to execute in one atomic invocation across all paths, enforced at both launcher and analyzer layers to prevent race conditions or stale UUID deletion from multi-pass operations. This design allows developers to query across sibling or reference repositories while keeping those repositories read-only and avoiding launcher project state pollution.
knowledge/concepts/project-extra-codegra.summary: Project-extra codegraph paths index additional read-only directories into a project's codegraph without registering them as launcher projects. The critical invariant: `--prune-stale` must run as a single analyzer invocation combining the primary repo and all extras via unified `--extra-path` flags and a shared `visited_uuids` set across all sources, enforced at both the launcher and analyzer layers to prevent multi-pass corruption.

knowledge/concepts/prompt-engineering-fu.title: Prompt Engineering — Fundamentals (2026)
knowledge/concepts/prompt-engineering-fu.description: Prompt Engineering — Fundamentals (2026) teaches core patterns for prompting modern LLMs using a three-pillars model: context provision, instruction clarity, and constraint definition. The most empirically effective techniques are Chain-of-Thought (reduces reasoning errors ~60%), few-shot learning, and role-based prompting; Claude 4.x models require explicit instructions rather than implicit ones, with motivation stated and "above and beyond" behavior explicitly requested. Implementation follows fundamental rules: prioritize clarity and specificity over verbosity, keep prompts focused on one task, and iterate through testing and refinement. Use this when building any LLM application to maximize accuracy, reliability, and consistency across different model tiers.
knowledge/concepts/prompt-engineering-fu.summary: Effective prompts follow three pillars—context, clarity, constraints—with Chain-of-Thought reducing reasoning errors ~60%; crucially, Claude 4.x models require explicit rather than implicit instructions and stated motivation, defaulting to literal task completion rather than inferring unstated goals.

knowledge/concepts/prompt-engineering-mc.title: Prompt Engineering — MCP and Tool Design (2026)
knowledge/concepts/prompt-engineering-mc.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard adopted by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind for connecting LLMs to tools, prompts, and resources; this document covers prompt patterns for tool design and production security hardening. MCP exposes three orthogonal capabilities—Tools (function calls), Prompts (parameterized instruction templates), and Resources (URI-addressable data)—each requiring different prompt shapes because the model interacts with them differently. Tool-use prompts must include tool signatures, concise descriptions, trigger conditions ("when to use"), and return shapes; design rules recommend verb-first naming, documented return structures, inline "when to use" clauses, limiting to 10-15 tools per prompt (50+ degrades selection accuracy), and filtering out unavailable tools. Proper MCP prompt design improves tool selection accuracy and is essential for production systems where reliable tool invocation depends on clear, actionable prompt structure.
knowledge/concepts/prompt-engineering-mc.summary: MCP exposes three orthogonal capabilities—Tools (function calls), Prompts (instruction templates), and Resources (read-only data)—each requiring distinct prompt structures; tool-use prompts must specify signatures, one-line descriptions with inline trigger conditions, return shapes, use verb-first naming, and limit to 10–15 tools for selection accuracy.

knowledge/concepts/prompt-engineering-mu.title: Prompt Engineering — Multi-Agent (2026)
knowledge/concepts/prompt-engineering-mu.description: Multi-agent prompt engineering defines patterns for LLM systems where specialized agents collaborate via orchestrator/specialist topologies and structured communication protocols. Two coordination models exist—orchestration (centralized coordinator decomposes and delegates to specialists) and agent-to-agent communication (lateral specialist communication using structured markers like [FINDING], [QUESTION], [BROADCAST]). System prompts establish each agent's expertise, communication protocol, and collaboration rules to enforce specialist behavior. Use multi-agent systems for parallelizable complex tasks requiring iterative refinement; avoid for simple linear problems where a single agent solves the task in 200 tokens, as multi-agent coordination adds overhead and regresses latency.
knowledge/concepts/prompt-engineering-mu.summary: Multi-agent prompt systems use three coordination topologies—orchestrator delegation, lateral agent-to-agent communication via shared protocols, and distributed planning (MARL-style with goal/state/action/observation maintenance)—but should only be applied to parallelizable, complex tasks; the litmus test is that if the goal fits in 200 tokens for one expert, single-agent is faster and higher quality.

knowledge/concepts/qlora.md.title: QLoRA
knowledge/concepts/qlora.md.description: QLoRA is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that combines 4-bit quantization of frozen base model weights with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapters trained in higher precision, enabling fine-tuning of 65B+ parameter LLMs on consumer hardware (single GPU with 48GB VRAM). The method uses NF4 quantization—a 4-bit format optimized for normally-distributed neural network weights—combined with double quantization of quantization constants and paged optimizers to manage memory constraints. Only small LoRA adapter weights (~0.1–1% of total parameters) are trained in BFloat16; the base model remains frozen and is dequantized on-the-fly during the forward pass. QLoRA dramatically reduces VRAM requirements (e.g., 65B model from 1040GB to 48GB), making large-scale model adaptation accessible to researchers without enterprise-scale infrastructure.
knowledge/concepts/qlora.md.summary: QLoRA combines 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization of the base model with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapters trained in BFloat16, reducing fine-tuning memory from 260GB to ~48GB for 65B parameter models and enabling training on single consumer GPUs. The breakthrough is storing frozen weights in 4-bit while training only small adapter matrices (~0.1–1% of parameters), matching full fine-tuning quality within 1–2% on instruction-following and alignment tasks.

knowledge/concepts/raft-consensus-algori.title: Raft Consensus Algorithm
knowledge/concepts/raft-consensus-algori.description: Raft is a consensus algorithm that ensures a cluster of nodes reaches agreement on a replicated state machine by decomposing the problem into three independent subproblems: leader election, log replication, and safety. It uses randomized election timeouts and a leader-based approach where the elected leader replicates log entries to followers; entries become committed once a majority acknowledges them, and formally proven safety properties guarantee at most one leader per term and consistency across the cluster. Unlike Paxos, Raft achieves understandability through asymmetric design—followers trust the leader—rather than symmetric peer-to-peer coordination. Use Raft for building fault-tolerant distributed systems (databases, key-value stores, consensus services) where strong consistency and practicality matter more than Byzantine fault tolerance.
knowledge/concepts/raft-consensus-algori.summary: Raft is a consensus algorithm that achieves the same crash-fault tolerance as Paxos (2f+1 nodes tolerating f failures) through stronger understandability via decomposition into leader election, log replication, and safety—using randomized election timeouts and term-based logical clocks to ensure only one leader per term and prevent stale leaders from being elected.

knowledge/concepts/rag-pattern.md.title: RAG Pattern
knowledge/concepts/rag-pattern.md.description: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is an LLM architecture pattern that grounds model responses in retrieved documents instead of relying on the model's parametric knowledge, decoupling the knowledge base from the model for cheap updates. The system embeds documents into a vector store, then embeds incoming queries to retrieve top-k relevant documents, which are incorporated into the prompt sent to the LLM. Pattern variants include Standard RAG (single retrieval), Iterative RAG (multiple reasoning rounds), Fusion RAG (query expansion), and Corrective RAG (quality validation with fallback to web search). Use RAG when knowledge changes frequently, answers must cite sources, domain knowledge is specialized, or factual precision is critical—it addresses the LLM's static knowledge cutoff and reduces hallucination through grounding.
knowledge/concepts/rag-pattern.md.summary: RAG grounds LLM responses in retrieved documents rather than parametric knowledge, decoupling the knowledge base from model weights so knowledge updates require no retraining. The pattern retrieves top-k relevant chunks from a vector store at query time and augments the LLM prompt with context—variants include iterative RAG (multi-hop reasoning), corrective RAG (quality-gated with web search fallback), and fusion RAG (multi-query expansion).

knowledge/concepts/read-image-memory-awa.title: read_image — Memory-Aware Vision-Model Gating
knowledge/concepts/read-image-memory-awa.description: `read_image` is an MCP tool that returns images as base64 data URLs and optionally runs a local vision model (qwen3.5:9b by default) to generate descriptions, with memory-aware gating to prevent OOM errors. It uses per-model VRAM and RAM thresholds (e.g., 7.5 GB VRAM for qwen3.5:9b), probes free memory at module load via nvidia-smi or psutil, and tiered resize budgets (1024² down to 256² pixels) based on available VRAM. If the chosen model doesn't fit, it auto-falls back to a smaller installed model; all probes fail conservatively to "no GPU + 8 GB RAM" defaults. Use when you need local image descriptions on constrained hardware or want to avoid uploading images to Claude's vision API.
knowledge/concepts/read-image-memory-awa.summary: The tool gates Ollama vision-model inference on VRAM/RAM thresholds (qwen3.5:9b requires 7.5 GB VRAM, with auto-fallback to smaller models) and clamps image resize by free VRAM tier (256²–1024² pixels), while always returning base64 data for Claude's native vision.

knowledge/concepts/reinforcement-learnin.title: Reinforcement Learning
knowledge/concepts/reinforcement-learnin.description: Reinforcement Learning is a machine learning paradigm where an agent learns to maximize cumulative reward by iteratively selecting actions in an environment and observing consequences, rather than learning from labeled data. The agent learns either a value function (expected cumulative reward per state) or a policy (state-to-action mapping) through trial-and-error, balancing exploration (trying new actions) and exploitation (using known good actions), controlled by discount factors and strategies like ε-greedy selection. Key algorithms split into value-based methods (Q-Learning, DQN) that estimate action values and derive policy from them, and policy-gradient methods (REINFORCE, PPO, A2C) that directly optimize the policy using gradient ascent. RL enables training in environments without labeled data (games, robotics, control) and is foundational to RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback), the technique used to align modern LLMs like ChatGPT and Claude to human preferences.
knowledge/concepts/reinforcement-learnin.summary: Reinforcement Learning trains agents to maximize discounted cumulative reward (G_t = r_t + γ·r_{t+1} + ...) through environment interaction, using value-based methods (Q-Learning, DQN), policy gradients (PPO, REINFORCE), or actor-critic hybrids; RLHF (supervised fine-tuning → reward model → PPO) aligns modern LLMs by optimizing against human-preference-trained reward models.

chunk_summaries.1.0: This chunk identifies distributional shift and value overestimation as offline RL's core problem: algorithms assign inflated Q-values to unseen actions encountered during bootstrapping, causing learned policies to diverge catastrophically from the training dataset.

knowledge/concepts/reproducible-research.title: Reproducible Research Workflows
knowledge/concepts/reproducible-research.description: Reproducible research means a third party can recover identical (or numerically-documented-tolerance) outputs using the same inputs, code, and environment—requiring four layers: environment pinning, data versioning, workflow orchestration, and deterministic randomness. Environment pinning uses language-specific lockfiles (uv/pixi for Python, renv for R, Project.toml for Julia, or Docker digests) to freeze dependencies; data versioning tracks file content via DVC, Git LFS, pooch, or S3 manifests paired with OSF/Zenodo DOIs for published datasets. Every data file must have a recorded content hash and provenance (URL or generating command), and workflows require explicit dependency graphs to prevent silent computation order changes. This matters for published research requiring DOI-backed archival, regulatory compliance, and long-term scientific trust—without these layers, code becomes unreproducible within months as dependencies drift and data links break.
knowledge/concepts/reproducible-research.summary: Reproducibility requires four layers: environment pinning (uv/pixi), data versioning (DVC/Git LFS), workflow DAGs (Snakemake/Nextflow), and deterministic randomness; the technology exists for each—the bottleneck is process coordination.

knowledge/concepts/reward-shaping-intrin.title: Reward Shaping & Intrinsic Reward Design in RL
knowledge/concepts/reward-shaping-intrin.description: Reward shaping modifies reward signals to accelerate RL learning while preserving the optimal policy, and reward engineering designs the initial reward function; together they address sparse/delayed rewards and alignment problems. Potential-based shaping uses R'(s,a,s') = R(s,a,s') + γ*Φ(s') - Φ(s) where Φ is a heuristic state-value function, mathematically guaranteeing the policy argmax remains unchanged because the shaped reward only shifts value functions by a constant. Practical designs use domain-specific potential functions (negative distance to goal in navigation, learned heuristics in robotics) and meta-learning approaches like PGRD and LIRPG to dynamically adjust reward parameters during training. Essential for overcoming sample inefficiency in sparse-reward domains like Minecraft and robotics, preventing reward hacking, and ensuring agent behavior aligns with designer intent.
knowledge/concepts/reward-shaping-intrin.summary: Potential-based reward shaping uses the formula R'(s,a,s') = R(s,a,s') + γ*Φ(s') - Φ(s) to accelerate RL learning while mathematically preserving the optimal policy through value function shifts. Intrinsic reward shaping combines extrinsic rewards with meta-learned intrinsic signals (curiosity, progress, diversity) to address sparse rewards and reduce sample complexity without manual reward design.

knowledge/concepts/rotary-positional-emb.title: Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE)
knowledge/concepts/rotary-positional-emb.description: Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE) encode token positions as rotations in 2D subspaces, unifying absolute and relative positional encoding with zero learnable parameters—the de facto standard for major open-weight LLMs like Llama, Mistral, and Qwen. RoPE applies rotation matrices to consecutive embedding dimension pairs with frequency θ_d = 1/base^(2d/|D|), ensuring query-key dot products depend only on relative token distance and enabling natural recency bias through frequency spread. The method incurs only 1-3% compute overhead and integrates seamlessly with FlashAttention, linear attention, and sparse variants—unlike relative bias methods requiring full N×N attention matrices. RoPE enables context-extension techniques (Position Interpolation, NTK-aware Interpolation) that scale training context from 4K to 2M+ tokens, making it essential for modern LLM scaling.
knowledge/concepts/rotary-positional-emb.summary: RoPE rotates consecutive embedding dimension pairs by position-dependent angles such that query-key dot products depend only on relative token distance, achieving true relative position encoding with zero learnable parameters. It is the de facto standard for all major open-weight LLMs (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) and enables context extension to 2M+ tokens via methods like YaRN, which combines NTK-aware interpolation with attention temperature scaling.

knowledge/concepts/saas-pricing-psycholo.title: SaaS Pricing Psychology for Solo Founders
knowledge/concepts/saas-pricing-psycholo.description: Pricing psychology framework for solo SaaS founders showing that 1% price increases drive ~10x more profit growth than 1% volume increases, applied to self-serve products in the $0–50K MRR range. The core technique is 3-tier Good–Better–Best with 1:2.5:6 price ratios—buyers avoid extremes and pick the middle tier as "reasonable"—preceded by anchoring (leading with highest price makes others seem like savings). The value metric (what you charge per—outcome, usage, seats, flat, or feature tiers) is the most critical decision; start simple with flat or seat pricing, add usage tracking later as you learn cost drivers. Critical for founders unconsciously underpricing with single plans; even modest optimizations to these levers yield compounding profit gains.
knowledge/concepts/saas-pricing-psycholo.summary: Pricing lever moves profit ~10× more than volume changes for solo SaaS founders; the core strategy is 3-tier anchoring with a 1:2.5:6 price ratio (designing the middle tier first as your target customer segment) combined with value-metric selection ranked by customer alignment (outcome > usage > seats > flat).

knowledge/concepts/saas-pricing-rollout-.title: SaaS Pricing Rollout Playbook
knowledge/concepts/saas-pricing-rollout-.description: A playbook treating pricing changes as controlled deployments, defining target audience, measurement plan, rollback criteria, and comms sequence rather than just the new price. For indie companies under $25K MRR, the default approach is grandfathering existing customers and charging new signups the new price—lowest-risk with zero churn from the change itself. Single-cutover rollouts are preferred over A/B testing for solo founders, since price tests require 1000+ visitors per variant weekly and fragment customer experience. Proper rollout execution prevents revenue leakage from botched deployments (churn, SEO mismatches, billing errors) that often exceed gains from the price change itself.
knowledge/concepts/saas-pricing-rollout-.summary: Pricing rollouts are deployments requiring a target audience, measurement plan, and rollback criterion; for indie SaaS under $25K MRR, the default lowest-risk strategy is "new signups only, grandfather existing customers indefinitely" measured over 8–12 weeks, which eliminates churn risk while capturing pure conversion/ARPU impact without the statistical burden of A/B testing.

knowledge/concepts/safe-install.md.title: Safe-Install — Content-Based Service Detection
knowledge/concepts/safe-install.md.description: `install.py` fingerprints HTTP responses from backing services (Weaviate, Ollama, code-embed) to detect whether each port hosts an orchestrator-managed service, a foreign service, or nothing—without relying on container names. It classifies services into four states (not running, vct-managed, foreign, incompatible) via port-specific probes: Weaviate checks `/v1/schema` for vct-prefixed collections, Ollama queries `/api/tags` against `services.toml`, and code-embed inspects `/health` for a matching model signature. When a foreign service is detected, three modes resolve conflicts: `alt-port` (safest, runs orchestrator on a free port), `adopt` (writes into the foreign service), or `abort`. An adoption lock in `~/.vct/services.toml` ensures the launcher and install.py agree on resolution, enabling safe coexistence with user-managed services on canonical ports without modification.
knowledge/concepts/safe-install.md.summary: `install.py` detects backing services via HTTP response fingerprinting to classify them as not-running, vct-managed, foreign, or incompatible, enabling safe coexistence with foreign services on canonical ports without modification. The `--on-conflict` flag resolves conflicts via alt-port (default), adopt, or abort modes, with state tracked in `~/.vct/services.toml`.

knowledge/concepts/saga-pattern-distribu.title: Saga Pattern for Distributed Workflows
knowledge/concepts/saga-pattern-distribu.description: The saga pattern coordinates workflows across multiple independent systems by executing local transactions with defined compensations that semantically undo effects if any step fails. Two orchestration styles exist: choreography (event-driven with services reacting to events, but scattered failure logic) and orchestration (central coordinator drives execution linearly, but requires a durable engine to survive crashes). Compensations are forward operations that undo effects (refunds, release reservations), not database rollbacks. Use sagas for multi-system workflows where distributed transactions are impossible; prefer orchestration with a durable engine (Temporal, Step Functions) in production to prevent mid-saga state corruption.
knowledge/concepts/saga-pattern-distribu.summary: Sagas coordinate distributed workflows using sequences of local transactions with compensations that semantically undo effects on failure. Production implementations require durable orchestrators like Temporal or Step Functions to maintain state across crashes and provide linear, recoverable code—naive choreography-based approaches scatter failure logic across services and become unmaintainable.

knowledge/concepts/sales-funnel-stages-2.title: Sales Funnel Stages and Bow-Tie Model 2026
knowledge/concepts/sales-funnel-stages-2.description: The bow-tie model extends the classic TOFU/MOFU/BOFU sales funnel by treating acquisition and retention as equally weighted operational sides, pivoting at contract close. The left side (acquisition) flows lead → opportunity → closed-won, while the right side (retention) flows onboarded → activated → renewed → expanded → referred, with conversion-rate benchmarks for each stage (e.g., 2–5% awareness-to-engaged for B2B SaaS). Modern SaaS economics depend on Net Revenue Retention (NRR) > 100%, meaning existing customers generate more revenue year-over-year than new cohorts, enabling a 120% NRR business to grow 1.2x with zero new sales. The classic funnel misses 60% of the customer lifecycle; use TOFU/MOFU/BOFU only for content planning, and adopt the bow-tie model as your operational framework to balance acquisition and expansion investment.
knowledge/concepts/sales-funnel-stages-2.summary: The bow-tie model extends the classic TOFU/MOFU/BOFU acquisition funnel through post-sales stages (onboarding, activation, expansion, advocacy), treating retention and acquisition as equally weighted; in SaaS, Net Revenue Retention (NRR) > 100% means existing customers compound revenue growth independently of new sales, making the right side of the bow-tie the primary economic engine.

knowledge/concepts/scientific-paper-tria.title: Scientific Paper Triage Schema
knowledge/concepts/scientific-paper-tria.description: A structured extraction schema converts a folder of scientific papers into a comparable table, enabling researchers to rapidly rank papers by relevance without cover-to-cover reading. The schema captures metadata (citation, DOI, study type), experimental design (population, sample size, controls, randomization, blinding), outcomes (effect sizes, p-values, primary claims), and critical flags (pseudoreplication risk, multiple-comparison corrections, preregistration status, data/code availability). All fields are documented explicitly—missing data is recorded as "NOT_REPORTED" rather than inferred. Use this to systematically triage large literature sets, identify methodological weaknesses that temper trust in claims, and prioritize papers for deeper study.
knowledge/concepts/scientific-paper-tria.summary: A structured extraction schema with 20+ fields (study type, sample size, randomization, blinding, effect size, preregistration, code availability) converts a folder of papers into a comparable table for rapid ranking by methodological rigor. The accompanying critical-appraisal checklist automatically flags pseudoreplication, missing effect sizes, uncorrected multiple comparisons, and missing data-sharing as disqualifiers, enabling researchers to triage dozens of papers in minutes instead of hours of cover-to-cover reading.

knowledge/concepts/semantic-search.md.title: Semantic Search
knowledge/concepts/semantic-search.md.description: Semantic search finds documents based on meaning rather than keyword matches by encoding queries and documents as dense vectors in an embedding space and retrieving documents with smallest vector distance. Documents and queries are embedded using models like qwen3-embedding or CodeSage-Large-v2 into high-dimensional vectors, then retrieved via nearest neighbor search using metrics like cosine similarity. Hybrid search combines semantic retrieval with sparse keyword matching (BM25) to capture both conceptual relevance and exact matches. This approach is critical for RAG systems and AI applications where different phrasings express the same concept, though it requires approximate nearest neighbor algorithms (HNSW) for performance at scale.
knowledge/concepts/semantic-search.md.summary: Semantic search retrieves documents by meaning rather than keyword matching, encoding both queries and documents as dense vectors in a shared embedding space and finding nearest neighbors via vector distance metrics like cosine similarity. This enables discovery of conceptually related content even when query and document use completely different terminology, unlike traditional lexical search.

knowledge/concepts/shared-knowledge-grap.title: Shared Knowledge Graph (Cross-Project)
knowledge/concepts/shared-knowledge-grap.description: The vibecoded orchestrator ships with a shared Weaviate knowledge graph collection (`VibeCodedOrchestrator_KnowledgeGraph`) seeded at install time and reused across all projects on a machine, eliminating the need to re-learn reusable knowledge (LoRA fine-tuning, transformer architecture, RAG patterns) per project. Every project queries both its own per-project KG and the shared collection; results are merged, de-duped, and re-ranked together by the MCP server. The shared collection is bootstrapped once via `install.py` Step 7d; reads are unconditional (always enabled), while writes and reads can be individually gated via `SHARED_KG_WRITE_DISABLED` and `SHARED_KG_READ_DISABLED` flags. This matters because new projects automatically inherit accumulated knowledge without per-project setup, creating a compound learning effect across the development environment.
knowledge/concepts/shared-knowledge-grap.summary: The vibecoded orchestrator maintains a shared Weaviate collection (`VibeCodedOrchestrator_KnowledgeGraph`) that every project queries alongside its per-project KG; all queries transparently merge, de-duplicate, and re-rank results from both collections via the weaviate_mcp server. Writing to the shared KG requires explicit `scope="shared"` in `store_knowledge_node()` calls, while reads are unconditional by default, preventing pollution while maximizing knowledge reuse across projects.

knowledge/concepts/sli-selection-methodo.title: SLI Selection Methodology
knowledge/concepts/sli-selection-methodo.description: SLI Selection Methodology is the judgment-based process for choosing the right Service Level Indicators for SLO design, as opposed to the mechanical burn-rate alerting math that follows. The process answers three foundational questions: who is the user, what does "service worked" mean to them, and what's measurable from your vantage point—then maps the answer to a service-type-specific SLI category (request-driven, storage, pipeline, streaming, or frontend) with primary and secondary indicators. Every SLI is expressed as `good_events / valid_events`, a ratio that directly plugs into SLO and alerting calculations. Wrong SLI choices cause either silent failures (alert stays green during outages) or alert fatigue (alert fires during normal operation, gets disabled), making this the critical bottleneck in building reliable monitoring.
knowledge/concepts/sli-selection-methodo.summary: SLI selection requires answering three foundational questions—who is the user, what does "worked" mean to them, and what's measurable—before designing metrics that map to burn-rate alerting via the good_events/valid_events ratio formulation. Most services require 2–3 layered SLIs (e.g., availability + latency + throughput) grouped by service shape (request-driven, storage, pipeline, streaming, frontend) to avoid alerting on wrong failure modes or missing real outages.

knowledge/concepts/slo-error-budget-mult.title: SLO Error Budgets and Multi-Window Multi-Burn-Rate Alerts
knowledge/concepts/slo-error-budget-mult.description:
**SLO Error Budgets and Multi-Window Multi-Burn-Rate Alerts**

An SLO error budget is the permitted failure rate inverse of a Service Level Objective (e.g., 0.1% for 99.9% uptime); multi-window multi-burn-rate alerts fire when the budget is consumed faster than sustainable across different observation windows. Burn rate measures current error rate divided by the error budget—a rate of 14.4 means the entire 30-day budget would exhaust in 2 days—enabling tiered alert severity (page alerts at 1h/5m windows, ticket alerts at 3d/6h windows). Recommended alert tiers use long windows to prevent flapping and short windows to detect recovery within minutes; Prometheus implements this via recording rules that pre-compute error rates across 5m, 1h, 6h time ranges. This approach fixes static threshold limitations: it catches slow budget leaks that static rules miss and avoids flapping on transient spikes while providing actionable urgency signals tied to actual SLO risk.
knowledge/concepts/slo-error-budget-mult.summary: SLO error budgets quantify acceptable failure (e.g., 0.1% for 99.9% SLO), and multi-window multi-burn-rate alerts fire when budget consumption exceeds the rate needed to exhaust it over the SLO window, with Google SRE recommending tiers at burn rates 14.4 (20h exhaust), 6 (5d), and 1 (10d) to avoid both false positives and false negatives. The core metric is burn rate = (current_error_rate) / (error_budget), which tells you how many SLO windows' worth of failure you're bleeding per unit time—replacing brittle static thresholds with precision tied to actual SLO risk.

knowledge/concepts/solo-saas-launch-play.title: Solo SaaS Launch Playbook
knowledge/concepts/solo-saas-launch-play.description: A coordinated multi-channel communication strategy for solo founders launching software releases, covering channel-specific conventions and messaging for public releases (v0.X, new features, milestones). The core narrative spine—problem → solution → user benefit—is adapted per channel (changelog with 5–20 bullets, blog post 300–700 words, Twitter thread 5–9 tweets), and a pre-flight heuristic ensures only user-visible changes warrant a full launch sequence. Prevents duplicated effort and strengthens credibility by forcing benefit-led messaging over feature-lists, so solo founders ship coordinated launches instead of scattered tweets.
knowledge/concepts/solo-saas-launch-play.summary: Solo SaaS launches coordinate multi-channel release communications (changelog, blog, tweets, email, in-app banner) around a consistent narrative spine: problem → shipped solution → user benefit. The critical failure pattern is omitting the problem statement; all successful launch comms lead with user benefit rather than feature lists, and channel-specific formatting (280 chars for tweets, 300–700 words for blog, etc.) is standardized by platform conventions.

knowledge/concepts/sow-contract-type-pla.title: SOW Contract-Type Playbook
knowledge/concepts/sow-contract-type-pla.description: A playbook defining four primary consulting SOW structures—T&M, fixed-price, retainer, and outcome-based—and the mandatory clauses required for each to prevent predictable disputes. Each type distributes risk differently: T&M shifts scope risk to the client but requires monthly caps and change-control; fixed-price requires objective (not subjective) acceptance criteria to prevent payment withholding; retainer demands explicit SLA definitions to avoid 24/7 on-call expectations; outcome-based ties payment to metrics the firm can actually move. The wrong contract type on wrong work produces guaranteed disputes—exploratory work on fixed-price creates overrun, T&M without caps creates runaway, outcome-based on unmovable metrics creates zero payment. Matching contract type to actual work scope is the single largest controllable factor in engagement margin and client satisfaction.
knowledge/concepts/sow-contract-type-pla.summary: Contract type determines which party absorbs scope-change risk and is the single largest controllable factor in engagement margin; the four primary types—T&M (client absorbs spend risk), fixed-price (firm absorbs delivery risk), retainer (shared utilization risk), and outcome-based (firm absorbs outcome risk)—each fail predictably when specific clauses are omitted (soft caps, objective acceptance criteria, SLAs, and outcome attribution respectively).

knowledge/concepts/sparse-activation.md.title: Sparse Activation
knowledge/concepts/sparse-activation.md.description: Sparse activation is a conditional computation mechanism that selectively activates a subset of neural network parameters per input, decoupling total parameter count from compute requirements. It uses input-dependent gating networks to dynamically route tokens through expert subnetworks; DeepSeek-V2 with 236B parameters activates only 21B per token, achieving 42.5% training cost reduction and 5.76x throughput over dense models. Two architectural variants exist: structured MoE sparsity (explicit expert selection) and activation sparsity (ReLU-induced zeros), where sparsity patterns can be dynamic (per-token varying) or static (post-pruning fixed). This technique is essential for efficient large-scale models because it enables expert specialization, better multi-task fine-tuning, and inference speeds comparable to much smaller dense models.
knowledge/concepts/sparse-activation.md.summary: Sparse activation selectively activates only a subset of neural network parameters per input (typically 5-28% for MoE models) through gating/routing networks, achieving parameter-compute decoupling where 236B-parameter models can operate at speeds comparable to 13-70B dense models. This conditional computation enables massive parameter scaling with reduced training cost (42.5% reduction in DeepSeek-V2) and increased throughput without proportional compute increases.

knowledge/concepts/speculative-decoding..title: Speculative Decoding
knowledge/concepts/speculative-decoding..description: Speculative decoding is a lossless inference acceleration technique for autoregressive LLMs that uses a small draft model to propose multiple tokens ahead, then validates them in parallel with a larger target model in a single forward pass, guaranteeing output identical to standard decoding. The draft model generates k tokens (typically 4–8), the target model processes all k tokens in one forward pass, and each drafted token is accepted based on probability ratio min(1, p_target(x_i) / p_draft(x_i)), with rejected tokens sampled from a residual distribution to maintain correctness. Speedup correlates with acceptance rate and averages 2–4× wall-clock time in practice, maximized on memory-bandwidth-bound hardware; recent variants like EAGLE-2 and EAGLE-3 achieve 3–6.5× speedup using trained draft models with dynamic speculation. It matters because it delivers substantial inference speedup without approximating the target model, making it essential for reducing latency in production LLM deployments.
knowledge/concepts/speculative-decoding..summary: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference 2-4× by running a draft model and target model in parallel—the draft proposes tokens, the target validates them in one forward pass using speculative sampling (accept with probability min(1, p_target/p_draft))—while remaining provably lossless: the output distribution exactly matches standard autoregressive decoding. EAGLE-3 extends this to 3-6.5× speedup using training-time testing and lightweight prediction heads.

chunk_summaries.1.0: Speculative decoding is a lossless inference acceleration technique where a small draft model proposes multiple tokens and the target model validates all proposals in a single forward pass using probabilistic acceptance/rejection that preserves output distribution.

knowledge/concepts/sre-incident-response.title: SRE Incident Response Playbook
knowledge/concepts/sre-incident-response.description: A four-phase playbook for coordinating active incident response, ensuring teams follow a structured process under pressure rather than improvising. The phases in strict order are Triage (confirm/scope/severity/assign IC in 5–10 min), Hypothesis (generate 3–5 theories before investigation), Mitigate (restore service before understanding cause), and Verify (confirm stability and exit). The process requires immediate communication (status page within 5 minutes), a scribe logging all actions with timestamps, and the IC coordinating while others debug. This structure is essential for preventing decision-paralysis, reducing false-alarm response time by 30+ minutes, and creating accurate post-mortem records.
knowledge/concepts/sre-incident-response.summary: The incident playbook is a four-phase sequence (Triage → Hypothesis → Mitigate → Verify) where mitigations are prioritized by reversibility, not by likelihood of cause; cheap, reversible fixes like rollback are attempted first to minimize MTTR.

knowledge/concepts/structured-output.md.title: Structured Output
knowledge/concepts/structured-output.md.description:
Structured Output constrains LLM generation to produce outputs conforming to a specific schema (JSON, XML, typed objects) rather than free-form text, enabling reliable programmatic use in downstream pipelines.

Implementation methods include API-level JSON Mode (valid but unvalidated), schema-constrained APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI with Pydantic), guided decoding at inference time (Outlines, vLLM), and prompt-based JSON extraction. Tool calling natively structures output as function parameters with defined schemas.

Use structured output to guarantee type safety, enable parsing without retry loops, and integrate LLM outputs directly into applications without error-prone text parsing.
knowledge/concepts/structured-output.md.summary: Structured Output forces LLMs to generate outputs conforming to specific schemas (JSON/XML/typed objects) for downstream automation; native API-level schema constraints are most reliable, while prompt-based extraction is least reliable.

knowledge/concepts/supply-chain-security.title: Supply-Chain Security — SLSA Levels, SBOM, and Sigstore
knowledge/concepts/supply-chain-security.description: Supply-chain security encompasses source, build, dependencies, and deployment stages; SLSA defines maturity levels for build provenance, SBOM lists artifact components, and Sigstore provides keyless signing and verification. SLSA Build track progresses from L1 (scripted, unsigned builds) through L2 (signed attestations on hosted platforms like GitHub Actions) to L3 (hardened, ephemeral environments with non-falsifiable provenance). SBOMs use CycloneDX (compact, security-focused) or SPDX (standardized, license-tracking) formats and should be generated at build time with tools like syft, then scanned for vulnerabilities using grype. Essential for defending against sophisticated supply-chain attacks (SolarWinds, Log4Shell, xz-utils); Build L2 should be a baseline target and covers most common threat vectors.
knowledge/concepts/supply-chain-security.summary: SLSA defines build maturity in tiers (Build L2 with signed provenance attestations covers most supply-chain attacks); Sigstore replaces long-lived key management with keyless signing via short-lived OIDC certificates recorded in public transparency logs, eliminating the key-leak attack surface that plagued traditional code-signing.

knowledge/concepts/tauri-windows-create-.title: Tauri Windows CREATE_NO_WINDOW subprocess pattern
knowledge/concepts/tauri-windows-create-.description: Tauri/Win32 GUI apps on Windows spawn visible console windows for child processes because `CreateProcessW` allocates new consoles to GUI parents by default, causing visual flashing cascades that users perceive as crashes. The fix is a centralized `CommandExt` trait with a chainable `.silent()` method that applies the `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` flag (0x08000000) to both `std::process::Command` and `tokio::process::Command`. The trait must consume `self` and return `Self` (not `&mut self`) to avoid lifetime errors, enabling clean one-liner usage: `Command::new("git").silent().arg("status").output()?` This pattern scales across hundreds of call sites better than inline flag-setting, making it essential for Tauri apps spawning multiple concurrent subprocesses on Windows.
knowledge/concepts/tauri-windows-create-.summary: Tauri Windows GUI apps compiled with `windows_subsystem = "windows"` allocate visible conhost.exe console windows for all spawned subprocesses by default because `CreateProcessW` inherits the parent's console allocation; the fix is a chainable `CommandExt::silent()` trait method that sets the `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (0x08000000) creation flag, enforced via CI gate to prevent regressions.

knowledge/concepts/technical-debt-accoun.title: Technical Debt Accounting
knowledge/concepts/technical-debt-accoun.description: Technical Debt Accounting is a framework for quantifying and communicating technical debt to non-technical stakeholders so it can be budgeted and prioritized alongside other business decisions. It categorizes debt into four classes—deliberate (knowingly incurred with paydown triggers), inadvertent (discovered after the fact), bit-rot (environment-induced decay), and discovered (surfaced by incidents or audits)—each with different cost shapes and remediation strategies. Quantification uses time-to-fix estimates (adjusted for engineer under-estimation by 2–3×) or interest-rate framing (velocity tax in days per sprint). Without accounting, technical debt remains an invisible drag that loses budget negotiations to business opportunities; with it, teams can make honest trade-off decisions between paying down debt, refinancing it, or accepting it.
knowledge/concepts/technical-debt-accoun.summary: Technical Debt Accounting classifies debt into four types (deliberate, inadvertent, bit-rot, discovered) and quantifies each using time-to-fix and customer-impact mapping to convert invisible engineering concerns into measurable trade-offs that non-technical stakeholders can evaluate against competing budget priorities. Without accounting, tech debt loses every negotiation to sales and support issues; with it, the organization can decide whether to pay down, refinance, or accept the debt on honest merits.

knowledge/concepts/terraform-plan-review.title: Terraform Plan Review Discipline
knowledge/concepts/terraform-plan-review.description: Terraform plan review is a discipline focused on catching blast-radius surprises and invisible coupling in proposed state transitions—distinct from writing HCL, it examines whether a change will disrupt dependents or cause data loss. Plans render five action symbols with different risk profiles; the `-/+` (replacement) symbol on stateful resources like RDS or S3 is the leading cause of production outages and demands verification of snapshot/deletion-protection paths. Terraform's implicit `depends_on` graph means changes cascade silently through security groups, IAM roles, launch templates, and route tables, affecting in-flight traffic during the apply—the plan output does not show these dependencies, so reviewers must manually identify them. Plan review is mandatory before any production apply because the diff alone is blind to dependent resources and the true blast radius of a change.
knowledge/concepts/terraform-plan-review.summary: Terraform plan review consists of three ordered audits: action audit (reading change symbols), blast-radius audit (tracing implicit dependents through the reference graph), and drift audit (detecting state-reality mismatches). The replace symbol `-/+` on stateful resources (RDS, EBS, S3, persistent disks) is the single most common cause of production outages from routine applies and requires explicit data-loss verification (snapshots, deletion protection, cross-region replicas) before apply.

knowledge/concepts/transformer-architect.title: Transformer Architecture
knowledge/concepts/transformer-architect.description: The Transformer is a neural network architecture using self-attention to process sequences in parallel, capturing long-range dependencies; modern LLMs are predominantly decoder-only variants with causal masking. Self-attention computes Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax((Q×K^T)/√d_k)×V with O(n²) complexity, while multi-head attention applies this across different representation subspaces simultaneously. Position information must be explicitly encoded via methods like RoPE (Rotary Positional Embeddings), which encodes position as rotation with zero learnable parameters and is now standard across Llama, Mistral, and similar models. KV cache efficiency during autoregressive generation is critical for scaling; variants like GQA (Grouped-Query Attention) and MLA balance model quality against inference speed and memory constraints that grow linearly with sequence length and batch size.
knowledge/concepts/transformer-architect.summary: Self-attention with Query-Key-Value matrices enables parallel sequence processing with O(n²) complexity; KV cache memory growth is the primary bottleneck for decoder-only LLM inference (GPT/Llama/Claude), addressed by efficiency variants like Grouped-Query Attention and Mixture of Experts, with rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) now standard.

knowledge/concepts/tree-of-thought.md.title: Tree-of-Thought
knowledge/concepts/tree-of-thought.md.description: Tree of Thoughts (ToT) is a prompting framework that extends chain-of-thought reasoning by enabling language models to explore multiple reasoning paths simultaneously through tree search, where each node represents an intermediate problem-solving step. The framework decomposes problems into "thoughts" (coherent reasoning passages) and uses thought generators to produce candidate next steps—either sampled independently for diversity or proposed sequentially for coherence—combined with state evaluators that score or compare paths. Tree traversal employs search strategies including breadth-first search for small problems, depth-first search for larger trees, and beam search to balance quality and computational efficiency. ToT dramatically improves performance on complex reasoning tasks requiring backtracking: Game of 24 achieved 74% success with GPT-4 versus 4% with standard CoT, making it essential for multi-step problems where single linear reasoning paths fail.
knowledge/concepts/tree-of-thought.md.summary: Tree-of-Thought (Yao et al., NeurIPS 2023) extends chain-of-thought prompting by framing problem-solving as tree search where the model generates, evaluates, and searches through multiple intermediate reasoning paths ("thoughts") rather than a single left-to-right chain. On complex reasoning tasks like Game of 24, ToT achieves 74% success with GPT-4 versus 4% for standard CoT, using depth-first, breadth-first, or beam search strategies to explore the most promising reasoning branches.

knowledge/concepts/typography-system-des.title: Typography System Design
knowledge/concepts/typography-system-des.description: A typography system defines how a brand manages fonts across licensing, accessibility, performance, and visual identity by selecting families, establishing scales, and documenting line-heights and weights. The modern standard is either one display + one text family or a single superfamily with optical variants; type scales use a fixed ratio (1.125–1.618) to generate 7–10 documented steps with line-height varying by size (display 1.1–1.25, body 1.4–1.6, caption 1.5–1.7). Candidate pairings must be tested in two contexts—body size (long paragraph for readability) and display size (real headline at largest size for presence)—before committing, since many pairings fail at one size. Properly designed typography systems prevent licensing disasters, ensure readable layouts across all contexts, and catch pairing failures that would otherwise collapse when used with real content.
knowledge/concepts/typography-system-des.summary: Production typography systems use either a one display + one text family or a single optical-size superfamily, paired with a modular scale (7–10 steps from ratios like 1.2–1.618) and per-step line-height values (1.1–1.25 for display, 1.4–1.6 for body). Font licensing is the dominating constraint with recurring costs and must surface at brief time, not handoff.

knowledge/concepts/update-resume-require.title: Orchestrator Update Resume — Bug A (v0.2.51)
knowledge/concepts/update-resume-require.description: A bug fix for the orchestrator launcher's "Update" flow that halted when git merge/rebase conflicts occurred, leaving users with merged code but stale binary versions after manual conflict resolution. The fix introduces a resume sentinel (JSON checkpoint tracking conflict state), status detection identifying incomplete merges, and a Tauri resume command that validates preconditions (no in-flight merge state, HEAD advanced past conflict SHA, no unresolved markers) before re-running installation. A mutex prevents race conditions on rapid UI clicks, and a new highest-priority purple badge with pulse animation alerts users to continue the update. Critical for allowing users to complete interrupted orchestrator updates after manually resolving git conflicts, preventing divergence between on-disk source and the running binary.
knowledge/concepts/update-resume-require.summary: v0.2.51 fixes orchestrator updates halting mid-stream on git conflicts: users could resolve conflicts manually but the launcher had no mechanism to resume install.py, leaving merged source on disk but stale binaries running. The fix adds a resume sentinel at `.claude/state/orchestrator-update-resume-needed.json` with a `resume_orchestrator_update` command that validates conflict marker absence, HEAD advancement, and in-flight merge state before re-invoking install.py.

knowledge/concepts/use-red-four-golden-s.title: USE, RED, and Four Golden Signals — Observability Method Selection
knowledge/concepts/use-red-four-golden-s.description: Three complementary observability methods address different system layers: USE (Utilization/Saturation/Errors) for resources, RED (Rate/Errors/Duration) for request services, and Four Golden Signals for user-facing systems. USE metrics track CPU, memory, and network at the host layer; RED instruments request-driven services with histograms (never gauges) for latency percentiles; both apply at each layer to answer whether failures stem from resource constraints or application logic. USE acts as the observability floor—resource saturation blocks all application-level fixes, making it the prerequisite diagnosis before optimizing app behavior. Apply USE and RED together to every service for complete coverage across the stack.
knowledge/concepts/use-red-four-golden-s.summary: USE method instruments resource metrics (utilization, saturation, errors) on the host layer; RED instruments request metrics (rate, errors, duration) for request-driven services; Four Golden Signals combine these with saturation monitoring for user-facing systems. Saturation is the critical early-warning signal that predicts downstream latency and error degradation before users are affected—making it the most important metric to alert on across all three frameworks.

knowledge/concepts/vision-language-model.title: Vision-Language Models
knowledge/concepts/vision-language-model.description: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are neural architectures that learn shared multimodal representations from image-text pairs, bridging computer vision and NLP to enable tasks requiring simultaneous understanding of visual and linguistic content. VLMs comprise three core components: a vision encoder (CLIP ViT, DaViT, or SigLIP) that processes images into feature vectors, a language model backbone (typically decoder-only LLMs like Llama or Qwen), and a projection layer (linear, MLP, Q-Former, or resampler) that bridges feature spaces. Modern VLMs use sequence-to-sequence generation where image tokens are prepended to text tokens and the LLM generates responses autoregressively, enabling both understanding tasks (VQA, grounding, OCR) and generation tasks (captioning, image-to-code). VLMs are essential for applications requiring simultaneous visual-textual processing—document understanding, chart analysis, scene text extraction, and visual reasoning—and enable deployment across open-weight model families ranging from 0.2B (Florence-2) to 72B (Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3) parameters.
knowledge/concepts/vision-language-model.summary: Vision-Language Models combine a vision encoder (typically CLIP ViT) and an LLM backbone (Llama, Qwen) through projection layers, prepending compressed image tokens to text sequences for end-to-end multimodal tasks like VQA, captioning, and OCR. Current SOTA open-source models (Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3, Florence-2) scale 0.2B–78B parameters with VRAM requirements from 4GB to 24GB+, using quantization and dynamic resolution to optimize for specific tasks like document understanding and scene text extraction.

knowledge/concepts/webhook-security-chec.title: Webhook Security Checklist
knowledge/concepts/webhook-security-chec.description: Webhooks are HTTP requests from external services that trigger system actions; they present a wide attack surface because attackers can forge events impersonating legitimate providers. HMAC signature verification is mandatory—validate the raw request body against a shared secret using constant-time comparison before processing any webhook data. Additional layers include timestamp validation (reject events >5 minutes old), IP allowlisting to provider-published ranges, and idempotency checks on event IDs to prevent duplicate processing. Without these controls, attackers can forge transactions, replay events for duplicate work, exhaust resources, or inject malicious payloads.
knowledge/concepts/webhook-security-chec.summary: Webhook receivers must verify HMAC signatures using constant-time comparison against the raw request body before any processing, then layer defenses with timestamp validation (5-minute tolerance), IP allowlisting, and strict schema validation to mitigate forgery, replay, DoS, and injection attacks from anyone on the internet who discovers the endpoint URL.

knowledge/concepts/webkit-egl-preflight-.title: WebKit EGL Pre-Flight Probe
knowledge/concepts/webkit-egl-preflight-.description: A Linux startup probe that detects WebKitGTK's GBM/EGL failure before Tauri spawns its webview and conditionally disables the DMABUF renderer only when necessary. The failure occurs when NVIDIA proprietary userspace libraries are upgraded without kernel module reload, causing `eglInitialize()` to return `EGL_NOT_INITIALIZED` and crash the launcher at startup. The probe is self-healing—it re-runs at every launch and automatically restores GPU acceleration once the underlying driver state is fixed. This approach preserves performance on healthy systems, whereas setting the environment variable unconditionally would permanently disable GPU-accelerated rendering for all NVIDIA users.
knowledge/concepts/webkit-egl-preflight-.summary: Detects WebKitGTK's GBM/EGL initialization failure (primarily from mismatched NVIDIA drivers post-update) by pre-flight testing `eglInitialize()` and conditionally setting `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` only when failure is imminent, preserving GPU acceleration on healthy systems. Self-healing: re-evaluates every launch, automatically restoring the fast DMABUF path once the underlying driver state is fixed.

knowledge/models/codesage-large-v2.md.title: CodeSage-Large-v2
knowledge/models/codesage-large-v2.md.description: CodeSage-Large-v2 is a Salesforce code-embedding encoder that generates 2048-dimensional embeddings for source-code retrieval and similarity tasks across multiple programming languages. The 1.3B-parameter transformer model runs exclusively on GPU via sentence-transformers and is wrapped in a FastAPI service (listening on port 11440) that integrates embeddings into Weaviate code-graph collections. The orchestrator selects it automatically during install on CUDA-capable systems; CPU-only hosts fall back to the jina alternative. It delivers competitive performance against OpenAI's text-embedding-3-large on standard code-retrieval benchmarks (CoSQA, AdvTest), carries Apache 2.0 licensing, and provides higher-dimensional embeddings (2048) than fallback models for fine-grained code retrieval.
knowledge/models/codesage-large-v2.md.summary: CodeSage-Large-v2 (1.3B parameters, 2048-dim output) is the orchestrator's primary code-embedding encoder for GPU systems, deployed via FastAPI/sentence-transformers on port 11440. GPU-only in practice, it powers code-graph retrieval in Weaviate collections via the named vector `codesage_embed`.

chunk_summaries.1.0: CodeSage-Large-v2 is a 1.3B-parameter Salesforce code-embedding model producing 2048-dimensional embeddings for source-code retrieval, deployed as the orchestrator's primary GPU-accelerated code embedder via a FastAPI service bound to Weaviate code-graph collections.

knowledge/models/gemma4-e4b.md.title: Gemma 4 E4B
knowledge/models/gemma4-e4b.md.description: Gemma 4 E4B is Google DeepMind's edge-optimized variant of Gemma 4, an instruction-tuned multimodal model (text + image) sized for laptop and mobile deployment while retaining advanced capabilities like configurable thinking and native function-calling. At 9.6 GB quantized (q4_K_M), it operates with 128K context and requires approximately 5 GB VRAM and 8 GB system RAM as practical minimums. The orchestrator uses it as the primary KG-summary fallback when Claude CLI is unavailable and the host cannot run the larger Qwen 3.5 (9B). It matters as the go-to low-power summarization model for mid-range and resource-constrained machines, providing a non-Qwen alternative within the local inference stack.
knowledge/models/gemma4-e4b.md.summary: Gemma 4 E4B (9.6 GB, 128K context, ~5 GB VRAM at q4_K_M) is Google DeepMind's edge-class multimodal model that serves as the orchestrator's primary fallback for KG-summary generation on mid- and low-power machines when Claude CLI is unavailable. It supports native function-calling, configurable thinking, and image inputs across all tier sizes.

knowledge/models/jina-embeddings-v2-base.title: Jina Embeddings v2 Base Code
knowledge/models/jina-embeddings-v2-base.description: `jina-embeddings-v2-base-code` is a code-specific embedding model from Jina AI serving as the CPU fallback for code embeddings on hosts lacking CUDA GPUs. The 161M-parameter JinaBert model generates 768-dimensional embeddings with 8192-token context, trained on GitHub code and 150M+ code Q&A/docstring pairs across 30+ programming languages. It runs via Ollama (`unclemusclez/jina-embeddings-v2-base-code:latest`) and integrates into Weaviate as the `ollama_code_embed` named-vector slot when `CODE_EMBED_BACKEND=ollama` is configured. It balances CPU feasibility with code-aware pretraining and sufficient context length for function/module-sized chunks, making it the practical fallback for CPU-only deployments.
knowledge/models/jina-embeddings-v2-base.summary: Jina Embeddings v2 Base Code (161M params, 768-dim, 8K tokens) is the orchestrator's CPU fallback for code embeddings, trained on GitHub code and 150M+ code Q&A/docstring pairs across 30+ languages. Deployed via Ollama, it enables practical incremental code-graph indexing on GPU-less hosts.

knowledge/models/qwen3-embedding.md.title: Qwen3 Embedding
knowledge/models/qwen3-embedding.md.description: Qwen3 Embedding is Alibaba's dense text-embedding model family; the 8B variant ranked #1 on the MTEB multilingual leaderboard (June 2025, score 70.58). The orchestrator deploys the 0.6B variant (639 MB, 1024-dim embeddings, 32K context), requiring num_ctx=8192 via Ollama to surface full quality. It serves as the primary embedder in Weaviate MCP, registered as the `qwen3_embed` named vector for all knowledge-graph and document indexing; it coexists with the legacy `snowflake-arctic-embed2` embedder for backward compatibility. Use it for superior multilingual performance and Qwen stack integration while maintaining schema-compatibility with existing infrastructure.
knowledge/models/qwen3-embedding.md.summary: Qwen3 Embedding is Alibaba's text-embedding family with the 8B variant ranking #1 on MTEB's multilingual leaderboard (June 2025, 70.58). The orchestrator deploys the 0.6b variant (639 MB, 1024-dim, 32K context) as its primary text embedder via Ollama, supporting configurable output dimensions and replacing legacy Snowflake embeddings in the `qwen3_embed` named vector.

knowledge/models/qwen3.5.md.title: Qwen3.5
knowledge/models/qwen3.5.md.description: Qwen3.5 is a unified open-source multimodal foundation model from Alibaba that consolidates text and vision into a single checkpoint, replacing the separate Qwen3 and Qwen3-VL models. The family offers dense and sparse MoE variants from 0.8B to 122B parameters; the orchestrator targets `qwen3.5:9b` (6.6 GB, ~9 GB VRAM at q4_K_M) with a shared 256K context window across all sizes. Deployed locally for KG-summary generation as a fallback when Claude CLI is unavailable, it uses early-fusion multimodal training to handle both text and image inputs efficiently. It matters because unifying text + vision in one model cuts disk footprint in half, the 256K context eliminates RAG for most documents, and Apache 2.0 licensing aligns with the orchestrator's local-first stack.
knowledge/models/qwen3.5.md.summary: Qwen3.5 is a unified multimodal foundation model from Alibaba (0.8B–122B dense/MoE variants, 256K context) that consolidates separate Qwen3 text and Qwen3-VL vision models into a single Apache 2.0–licensed checkpoint. The orchestrator defaults to qwen3.5:9b for local KG-summary generation, requiring ~9 GB VRAM at q4_K_M quantization on GPU hosts with ≥16 GB VRAM.

knowledge/models/snowflake-arctic-embed2.title: Snowflake Arctic Embed 2.0
knowledge/models/snowflake-arctic-embed2.description: Snowflake Arctic Embed 2.0 is a multilingual, sub-1B-parameter text-embedding model designed for enterprise retrieval on resource-constrained hosts, serving as the primary embedder on low-resource install profiles and a compatibility vector for content embedded before platform migrations. The model has 568M parameters with 1024-dimensional embeddings (1.2 GB, 8K context), with a 4096-token chunk budget for retrieval optimization; the orchestrator maintains it as an `ollama_embed` named vector alongside newer embedders (e.g., Qwen3) to ensure backward compatibility with older embedded content. Use Arctic Embed 2.0 when targeting hosts with ≤8 GB VRAM for low-footprint text search, or to preserve searchability of legacy embeddings during embedder migrations.
knowledge/models/snowflake-arctic-embed2.summary: Snowflake Arctic Embed 2.0 is a 568M-parameter, 1024-dimensional multilingual embedding model (1.2 GB) that serves as the active text embedder on the orchestrator's low-resource install profile and as a compatibility slot for legacy embedded content. It delivers enterprise retrieval throughput on hardware with ≤8 GB VRAM through a 4K-token chunk budget, maintaining searchability of arctic-embedded entries on projects that migrate to Qwen3.

knowledge/patterns/wear-the-hat-pattern..title: Wear-the-Hat Pattern (Role and Discipline Impersonation)
knowledge/patterns/wear-the-hat-pattern..description: The Wear-the-Hat Pattern is a parametric agent specification that adopts a named perspective (role, discipline, or domain) per invocation, activated via a user-supplied hat key that sets characteristic vocabulary, knowledge bounds, and methods. It reduces maintenance burden from O(hats) to O(1) by allowing new roles/disciplines to be added with one-line table edits, enabling cross-disciplinary translation where consultation is framed in domain-specific terms rather than generically. Different perspectives reveal different problems: a CTO and junior engineer reviewing the same artifact from their respective seats catch distinct bugs and gaps that same-seat review would miss. Apply this pattern when multiple specialties share a common workflow but differ in vocabulary/methods, when drafting as a specific role for external review, or for cross-disciplinary translation within a single session.
knowledge/patterns/wear-the-hat-pattern..summary: The Wear-the-Hat Pattern is a parametric agent design where a single specification adopts named perspectives (roles, disciplines, archetypes) via a hat-key parameter, collapsing maintenance from O(hats) to O(1) by using a lookup table to map shorthand keys to role-specific configurations (vocabulary, knowledge bounds, default methods). It's most useful for cross-disciplinary translation, role-based draft generation for review from different seats, and coverage of perspective-specific bugs that reviewers in other roles would miss.

knowledge/tools/claude-code-cli-headless.title: Claude Code CLI - Headless & Scripted Usage
knowledge/tools/claude-code-cli-headless.description: Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`) enables headless/programmatic use by wrapping the active claude.ai login, allowing cost-free orchestration under Claude Max subscriptions—unlike the Agent SDK which requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and charges per token. Core flags control output format (`--output-format stream-json`), sessions (`--resume`, `--continue`, `--fork-session`), and context injection (`--append-system-prompt` preserves defaults; `--system-prompt` replaces entirely). Tool access is fine-grained via `--tools`, `--allowedTools` (with glob patterns), and `--permission-mode` to skip interactive permission prompts. Use this pattern to wrap orchestration workflows in subprocesses without per-token API billing or interactive prompts.
knowledge/tools/claude-code-cli-headless.summary: Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`) provides cost-free headless execution via Claude Max subscription (unlike the per-token-billed Agent SDK), with flags for session resumption (`--resume`), tool restriction (`--allowedTools`), and real-time JSON streaming (`--output-format stream-json`).

knowledge/tools/claude-code-mcp-configur.title: Claude Code MCP Configuration Pattern
knowledge/tools/claude-code-mcp-configur.description: Claude Code MCP Configuration Pattern describes how to set per-project environment for MCP servers without leaking settings across projects on the same machine. The canonical channel is `.claude/settings.json` `env` block, which propagates to MCP subprocesses across all Claude Code surfaces (CLI, Desktop, VS Code extension) and all OSes, while machine-invariant MCP registrations live in `~/.claude.json` mcpServers. A critical footgun is `.vscode/settings.json` `claude-code.env`, which does NOT propagate to MCP subprocesses on Linux, causing silent fallback to bundled defaults instead. Developers must use `.claude/settings.json` `env` for reliable per-project configuration and can verify correctness via MCP startup logs showing resolved collections and their resolution source.
knowledge/tools/claude-code-mcp-configur.summary: Per-project MCP environment variables (KG_COLLECTION, CODE_GRAPH_PROJECT, etc.) must go in `.claude/settings.json` `env`—the only channel that propagates to MCP subprocesses across all Claude Code surfaces—not `.vscode/settings.json` `claude-code.env`, which silently fails on Linux despite appearing correct in workspace settings.

knowledge/tools/comfyui.md.title: ComfyUI
knowledge/tools/comfyui.md.description: Node-based image-generation interface for designers where workflows are JSON files — enabling perfect reproducibility, version control, and shareable configurations. Built on Python/PyTorch with a browser-based drag-and-drop editor; chains models, LoRAs, ControlNets, and IP-Adapters with efficient VRAM management and runs locally or headless. Provides core nodes (loaders, conditioning, samplers, latent/image ops) plus a large ecosystem of custom nodes for face restoration, video, animation, upscaling, regional prompting. Preferred over alternatives (Automatic1111, ForgeUI, online services) because workflows are reproducible across months, composable with new techniques, and integrable into automated asset pipelines.
knowledge/tools/comfyui.md.summary: ComfyUI is a node-based image-generation system (Python/PyTorch backend, browser editor) that serializes workflows as JSON for exact reproducibility and version control. It enables composable conditioning chains (LoRAs, ControlNets, IP-Adapters) with extensive custom-node ecosystem, making it the production standard for designers needing shareable, reproducible workflows.
